BSCAN registers¶

Both designs use the same registers:

Register Write Read
USER1 Clock enable of the SEM and the monitor interface: 1 = the clock operates, 0 = stopped. 0 after programming. The value written last.
USER2 The ICAP grant of the SEM. 0 after programming. Basys 3: bit 0 = icap_grant. TE0841: bit 0 = cap_gnt, bit 1 = cap_rel. Basys 3: icap_request. TE0841: bit 0 = cap_req, bit 1 = cap_gnt.
USER3 The SEM status signals: 8 bits on the Basys 3, 10 bits on the TE0841 (see status_names in main.py).

On the Basys 3, the LEDs show icap_request (LD0), status_heartbeat (LD1), status_initialization (LD2) and SEM idle (LD15).

How the arbitration works¶

Each experiment does these steps:

  1. Program the design, start the clock (USER1 = 1) and set the ICAP grant to 1 (USER2 = 1). The SEM initializes and goes to observation.
  2. Send I. The SEM goes to idle: it stops scanning and does not use the ICAP.
  3. Stop the clock (USER1 = 0), inject the upsets of the experiment, start the clock again (USER1 = 1).
  4. Send O. The SEM goes back to observation, without a new initialization, and scans the CRAM.
  5. Show the injected bits, which of them the SEM reported, and the SEM status.

The clock is stopped during the injections because SK-RAFT injects a bit as a read-modify-write of the whole frame, through the same configuration logic that the SEM uses. With the clock stopped, the frame address in each report (PA - Physical Address) is the FAR of the injected frame.

The script does not reset the SEM (R 00). In observation, the SEM ignores R 00. A reset from idle works, but then the SEM initializes with the upsets in the CRAM, and it does not report them.

The experiments¶

The results are from runs with SEED 12, the default.

# Target Upsets Result on the Basys 3 Result on the TE0841
1 Anywhere One single bit upset (SBU) The SEM corrects the bit and reports it (SED OK, COR). The SEM corrects the bit and reports it (ECC, COR).
2 Anywhere Two adjacent bits in one word of a frame The SEM detects a double error (DED) and stops as uncorrectable. The SEM corrects both bits and reports them.
3 Anywhere Three bits in one frame, in different words The SEM cannot correct the frame. It corrects a wrong bit (word 89, bit 13), then reports CRC and stops as uncorrectable. The SEM cannot correct the frame. It reports COR without corrected bits, then stops as uncorrectable.
4 The SEM One SBU The SEM corrects the bit and reports it. The SEM corrects the bit and reports it.
5 The SEM NUM_SEM_UPSETS (1000) SBUs, one at a time: steps 2 to 4 for each SBU The SEM corrects 4 SBUs, then it stops answering (round 5: FAR 00400410, word 40, bit 21). The SEM corrects 6 SBUs, then it stops answering (round 7: FAR 00025907, word 114, bit 16).

"Anywhere" is a random CRAM bit of the device, outside pblock_sem (exclude_pblock of inject_random). "The SEM" is a random essential bit inside pblock_sem. Experiments 2 and 3 add the other bits to the frame of the first bit with inject_at.

Each experiment starts with a new programming of the FPGA, so that it starts from a clean CRAM. Experiment 5 stops when the SEM reports an uncorrectable error, does not answer O, or sends the same report LOOP_LIMIT times in one round. With the same seed, the script injects the same bits in every run: on the TE0841, two runs failed on the same bit. With other seeds, the SEM on the Basys 3 also failed after 9 corrected SBUs, or repeated a wrong correction without end (a correction loop). Its status signals did not show the fatal state (all state bits set).

Other results of the tests:

  • BRAM content. The SEM checks only the configuration frames (block type 0), so it cannot detect an upset in BRAM content (block type 1) and gives no report; the script prints a BRAM content bit: line for such picks. This includes the SEM's own BRAMs (three RAMB18E1 without ECC that hold its firmware and data buffer), so an upset there can silently change how the SEM works.
  • Matching. A report matches an injected bit if the word and the bit are the same. The script shows the PA of the matching report. A report that matches no injected bit is shown as "reported, not injected".

Requirements¶

  • SK-RAFT server, with the board connected through JTAG.
  • A USB-UART connection to the board (on the Basys 3, the USB cable gives JTAG and UART).
  • Vivado 2025.2 (the version that the Tcl scripts were written for) to build the design.
  • Python 3.9 or a later version, with the skraft package (api/python) and pySerial (pip install pyserial).

Generate the design¶

  1. Open the Vivado Tcl shell and run the script of your board, for example:
vivado -mode batch -source basys3/create_project.tcl

The script creates the project <board>/sem_arbitration/sem_arbitration.xpr next to itself, creates the SEM IP and opens the project in the Vivado GUI. 2. Run Generate Bitstream. The .bit and .ebd files go to <board>/sem_arbitration/sem_arbitration.runs/impl_1/. main.py reads them from there.

Run the example¶

  1. At the top of src/main.py, set BOARD and SK_RAFT_SERVER_IP.
  2. In BOARDS, set serial_number and uart_port for your board.
  3. Run the script:
python src/main.py
Constant Default Description
BOARD BOARDS["basys3"] The board: BOARDS["basys3"] or BOARDS["te0841"].
SK_RAFT_SERVER_IP / SK_RAFT_SERVER_PORT "127.0.0.1" / 50051 The address of the SK-RAFT server.
serial_number, uart_port (in BOARDS) for each board The serial number of the board (get_devices() gives the connected boards) and the COM port of its USB-UART.
EXPERIMENTS (1, 2, 3, 4, 5) The experiments to run, in this order.
SEM_PBLOCK "pblock_sem" The pblock of the SEM in the XDC files.
SEED 12 The seed of the random picks. With the same seed, each experiment hits the same bits in every run.
NUM_SEM_UPSETS 1000 The maximum number of rounds of experiment 5.
QUIET_S 1.0 A SEM reply is complete when the UART is silent for this time, in seconds.
WAIT_S 10.0 The maximum time for the SEM to initialize or to reply, in seconds.
REPORT_WAIT_S 0.5 After the reply to O, the time to wait for more SEM reports, in seconds.
LOOP_LIMIT 3 The number of identical SEM reports in one round that is a correction loop.

At the end, the script programs the FPGA again, so that the CRAM is correct. If the script stops before the end (an error or Ctrl+C), the CRAM is not correct. Program the FPGA again before you do other work.

Note on the TE0841 (UltraScale)¶

  • The script does not use USER2 bit 1 (cap_rel). With it, SK-RAFT can do the release handshake of PG187: set cap_rel, wait until cap_req is 0, then clear cap_gnt.

NEORV32 hardening: a hardened RISC-V core under SK-RAFT fault injection¶

Board Part License
Digilent Basys 3 xc7a35tcpg236-1 (Artix-7) Apache-2.0 (SolidKosmos code), BSD-3-Clause (NEORV32)

This example has a NEORV32 RISC-V SoC with SECDED and parity hardening, and a JTAG test harness for fault injection with SK-RAFT. The hardening protects the DMEM, the register file, the state of the CPU control FSM and the program counter. The HARDEN_EN generic selects a hardened or an unhardened build of the same design. Thus you can measure the effect of the hardening under fault injection.

The NEORV32 boots the CoreMark firmware from the IMEM image (BOOT_MODE_SELECT => 2). The image is in hw/neorv32/neorv32_application_image.vhd. Thus the bitstream holds the firmware, and you do not upload it separately.

Build and run the example¶

  1. From this folder, in the Vivado Tcl shell (or after settings64.bat / settings64.sh of Vivado), build the design: 
    vivado -mode batch -source create_project.tcl
    The script creates test_neo/test_neo.xpr from hw/ and builds it, from synthesis to bitstream (about 11 min on a laptop). Vivado writes the .bit, .ebd and .ll files to test_neo/test_neo.runs/impl_1/. The implementation run also runs the BRAM hold register pass (refer to "BRAM output latch protection"). The script prints the report of the pass, bram_hold_pass.rpt, which is in the same folder. The optional arguments are -tclargs [project_name] [project_dir] [-gui]. With -gui, the project opens in the Vivado GUI after the build.
  2. Run the campaign with neorv_fi_example/run_injection.py. Refer to its README. The script programs the FPGA and reads the UART at 500000 baud.

For the unhardened baseline, remove the # from this line near the end of create_project.tcl, and use a different project name:

# set_property generic HARDEN_EN=false [get_filesets sources_1]

The HARDEN_EN generic¶

The generic HARDEN_EN : boolean := true goes from neorv32_test_setup_bootloader through neorv32_top and neorv32_cpu to each modified file. With HARDEN_EN => false, the design operates as the stock NEORV32:

  • DMEM and register file (neorv32_dmem.vhd, neorv32_prim.vhd): the protected datapath and the plain datapath are in different generate branches. Thus a build with HARDEN_EN => false has no ECC hardware.
  • CPU control and frontend (neorv32_cpu_control.vhd, neorv32_cpu_frontend.vhd): the SECDED and parity logic stays in the design. The generic only masks its effect on the execution and on the interrupts.

Fault-injection test harness¶

The tester module connects three BSCAN USER registers to the cycle controller (clk_cycle_ctrlr). The cycle controller gates the NEORV32 clock.

Register Write Read
USER1 Design reset (active low) 32-bit status and CRC word
USER2 32-bit step-count command Current step count and status
USER3 Root clock enable (1 = on) The synchronized enable

The USER2 commands are:

  • A value other than 0 loads a cycle countdown.
  • 0x1 starts the countdown.
  • 0x2 cancels the countdown.

If the UART still sends data when the countdown ends, the controller keeps the clock on until the UART is idle (check_tx). The root clock goes to the NEORV32, the harness and the cycle controller. The root clock is off after programming. run_injection.py stops it during each injection.

BRAM output latch protection¶

Vivado makes the NEORV32 IMEM and DMEM from block RAMs. An SK-RAFT access to BRAM content frames (readback, inject, revert) overwrites the output latch of each block RAM port without an output register. The stored content does not change. Without protection, the core can use that wrong value instead of the word that it read before the freeze.

create_project.tcl sets the BRAM hold register pass (auxiliary_components/bram_hold_pass) as the hook before opt_design. The pass adds a register on the opposite clock edge behind each BRAM output in use. This register keeps the word that the core read before the freeze. After the build, examine bram_hold_pass.rpt. The report lists each block RAM and the change that the pass made. The clock gates of the harness are BUFGCEs. A BUFGCE stops low, as the pass requires.

The paths from a hold register to the logic on the BRAM clock edge have half a clock period. The paths from the register file BRAM through the ECC decoder and the ALU do not meet 70 MHz with half a period. Thus the default core clock is 40 MHz.

Firmware¶

sw/hardening_coremark/main.c is the part of the firmware that is specific to this design. It installs the fast-interrupt handlers of the hardening (DMEM and register file corrections, CPU control and frontend state, PC and RA parity). Then it runs CoreMark. The other files come from the NEORV32 sw/example/coremark/, with these changes in core_portme.c and core_portme.h:

  • The interrupts stay enabled during the timed run, so that the hardening interrupts can occur.
  • ITERATIONS is 3, for a short run.
  • The firmware does not print the floating-point results.
  • The UART runs at 500000 baud.
  • The firmware calculates a CRC over the printed characters.

To change the firmware, build it in NEORV32. Then replace hw/neorv32/neorv32_application_image.vhd with the image that NEORV32 makes.

Use another board¶

  1. Change part_name in create_project.tcl.
  2. Replace hw/xdc/basys3.xdc with the constraints of your board (clock, UART, GPIO and LED pins).
  3. For a different input clock, set CLK_IN_FREQUENCY and the clk_i period in the XDC. INTERNAL_CLOCK_FREQUENCY (default 40 MHz, refer to "BRAM output latch protection") is the core clock that clk_gen_wrapper makes from clk_i.
  4. Change harness_pblock in the XDC. Its slice range is for the xc7a35t.

Files¶

Path Contents
hw/neorv32/ NEORV32 files: core/, the top (neorv32_test_setup_bootloader.vhd) and the application image. THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md lists the modified files.
hw/src/ SolidKosmos sources: test harness, parity and SECDED blocks. The build adds the BSCAN files and clk_gen_wrapper from auxiliary_components/.
hw/xdc/ Basys 3 constraints (basys3.xdc).
create_project.tcl Creates the Vivado project, with the BRAM hold register pass from ../../auxiliary_components/bram_hold_pass/.
neorv_fi_example/ The SK-RAFT fault-injection campaign.
sw/hardening_coremark/ The firmware source that is specific to this design.
images/ The block diagram.

Known limits¶

  • The DMEM decoder (secded_dec8b) corrects from the syndrome only. It does not check the overall parity. Thus it can correct a double-bit error incorrectly.
  • The register file SECDED covers only the FPGA-style register file. It does not report a detected double-bit error yet. The ASIC-style register file (CPU_RF_HW_RST_EN) has no ECC.
  • HARDEN_EN => false does not remove the hardening logic of the CPU control and frontend (refer to "The HARDEN_EN generic").

NEORV32 fault-injection campaign¶

run_injection.py runs a fault-injection campaign on the NEORV32 hardening design. It measures the observed error rate (AVF) against a golden run. bscan_routine_helpers.py has the BSCAN register access (reset, step count, root clock, CRC read).

The calls of the example¶

Function Calls
Connection SkraftFpga.connect() and client.attach(), in with statements that release the device and close the connection
Design Design (.bit, .ebd, .ll, .xdc), dev.uploadDesignToServer() and dev.programFPGA(design)
Pblock exclusion exclude_pblock of dev.inject_random(): SK-RAFT does not inject into the harness pblock
BSCAN BscanPrimitive, dev.write_bscan() and dev.read_bscan()
Fault injection TargetMemory (essential bits, BRAM, FF, LUTRAM), dev.inject_random(), and dev.inject_at() to flip the bit back after the run

Run the example¶

Build the design first. Refer to the README of the example. The script reads the .bit, .ebd and .ll files from ../test_neo/test_neo.runs/impl_1/ (IMPL_DIR), and the XDC from ../hw/xdc/basys3.xdc. Set the constants at the top of the script, then run the script from this folder:

pip install ../../../api/python pyserial
python run_injection.py
Constant Default Description
SERIAL_NUMBER "210183BFD452A" The serial number of the board. get_devices() gives the connected boards.
UART_PORT "COM5" The serial port of the UART of the board.
TARGET "EBITS" The memory type of the campaign: "EBITS" (essential CRAM bits), "BRAM", "FF" or "LUT".
RUNS 200 The number of runs.
PROGRESS_EVERY 25 The script prints a progress line after this number of runs.

UART_BAUD (500000) must be equal to the baud rate of the firmware.

Run time¶

On the Basys 3, the attach, the programming and the golden run take about 1.5 min. Then one run takes about 1.8 s (TARGET = "EBITS"). The 200 runs of the default take about 6 min. A statistically useful AVF needs thousands of runs: for example, 14000 runs take about 7 h.

The script prints a progress line after each PROGRESS_EVERY runs, with the errors, the AVF and the time that is left. It prints a line for each run with a CRC difference (refer to "Result").

Stop the campaign¶

Press Ctrl+C at any time. The script stops at once, and prints and saves the results of the runs that completed. It does not count the run that Ctrl+C stopped. That run can leave an injected fault in the FPGA: program the FPGA again before you use the design.

The exit code is 0 when the campaign is done, 1 on an error and 130 after Ctrl+C.

Result¶

The script compares each run with the golden run on three CRCs: the CRC in the UART message, the CRC that the script calculates from the message, and the hardware CRC (USER1). If all three CRCs are different, the message gives the status:

Status Message
ERROR An exception report of the runtime (NEORV32-RTE)
DETECTED An [ALERT] and a wrong or missing crcfinal
SDC No [ALERT], and a wrong or missing crcfinal
HUNG One of the above, and the processor did not finish

The script does not count an [ALERT] with a correct crcfinal as an error. AVF = errors / runs.

A run with a CRC difference that is not an error shows as MISMATCH. For example, the hardware CRC is correct but the UART text that the script captured is incomplete, or an [ALERT] with a correct crcfinal. A MISMATCH is not an error and is not in the AVF. The summary gives the number of MISMATCH runs. Its HW CRC mismatches and UART mismatches lines count only the runs in which not all three CRCs differ.

injection_results/csvs/ has one line for each error, and the summary as the last line. injection_results/raw_data/ has the UART output of each run with a CRC difference, errors and MISMATCH runs.

Modified NEORV32 files¶

SolidKosmos S.A. modified the following NEORV32 files to add the hardening features used by this example design (SECDED/parity fault detection and correction, and test-harness hooks). Each file carries an inline "Modified by SolidKosmos S.A. (2026)" note immediately below its original NEORV32 header, describing the specific change. Everything outside of the noted change is original NEORV32 code and remains under NEORV32's copyright.

File Modification
hw/neorv32/core/neorv32_top.vhd Added a check_tx test-harness port; wired DMEM-ECC interrupt and regfile/frontend correction/parity flags into custom fast-interrupt lines. Added the top-level HARDEN_EN generic (default true), threaded to neorv32_cpu and neorv32_dmem.
hw/neorv32/core/neorv32_cpu.vhd Added a dmem_irq_i signal; latches/merges ECC-correction and parity/FSM flags into a custom fast-interrupt-request line. Threads HARDEN_EN to neorv32_cpu_frontend, neorv32_cpu_control, and neorv32_cpu_regfile.
hw/neorv32/core/neorv32_dmem.vhd Added per-byte-lane Hamming SEC encode/decode (secded_enc8b/secded_dec8b, one per byte, 12-bit codeword) and an irq_ecc_dmem output, gated behind HARDEN_EN (falls back to a plain unprotected byte-wide RAM when disabled). The decoder corrects based on syndrome only, without checking overall parity, so par_i/uncorr are unused -- it can't distinguish a single-bit from a double-bit error.
hw/neorv32/core/neorv32_cpu_regfile.vhd Added irq_ecc_o, sourced from the soft SECDED (secded_enc32b/secded_dec32b) in neorv32_prim_sdpram (FPGA-style register file only), gated behind HARDEN_EN; tied to '0' in the ASIC-style (RST_EN) register file, which has no ECC path.
hw/neorv32/core/neorv32_cpu_control.vhd Added SECDED (secded_enc4b/secded_dec4b) protection for the exe-engine FSM state, and parity generation/checking for PC/PC2/RA. Gated behind HARDEN_EN: when disabled, exe_fctv_state bypasses correction (direct passthrough of the raw state register) and the state-correction/PC-parity IRQ bits are masked out of custom_fast_irq.
hw/neorv32/core/neorv32_cpu_frontend.vhd Added parity generation/checking for the fetch-stage PC, and a one-hot weight detector on the fetch engine's own state register. Gated behind HARDEN_EN: check_o/ill_state_o are masked to '0' when disabled.
hw/neorv32/core/neorv32_uart.vhd Added a check_tx output used by the external clock controller to detect an in-flight/queued transmission.
hw/neorv32/core/neorv32_prim.vhd The neorv32_prim_sdpram entity only: added soft SECDED in fabric logic (secded_enc32b on the write data, one secded_dec32b on each read port) around the inferred block RAM, and an irq_ecc_o output that flags a corrected read, gated behind HARDEN_EN (falls back to the original inferred-BRAM behavioral description when disabled). Other primitives in this file are unmodified.
hw/neorv32/neorv32_test_setup_bootloader.vhd The top-level entity of this project. Instantiates the safe-startup PLL (clk_gen_wrapper) and the fault-injection test harness (tester), runs the NEORV32 on the gated clock of the harness, sends the GPIO output to the harness (CRC word) and the LEDs, and adds the HARDEN_EN and clock-frequency generics.
sw/hardening_coremark/main.c Adapted from NEORV32's sw/example/hello_world/main.c. Installs the custom fast-interrupt handlers for the hardening IRQs (see README.md) before handing off to CoreMark.

The HARDEN_EN generic¶

All of the SECDED/parity/ECC hardening added above is gated behind a single HARDEN_EN : boolean := true generic, exposed at every level from neorv32_test_setup_bootloader (the actual top-level entity used by this project) down through neorv32_top / neorv32_cpu to the individual modified files. Building with HARDEN_EN => false produces an unhardened baseline that should behave like stock NEORV32 for fault-injection comparisons: no SECDED/ parity/ECC hardware is left in a position to affect execution or report errors. Two exceptions to note:

  • In neorv32_dmem.vhd and neorv32_prim.vhd (regfile ECC), the protected and unprotected datapaths are separate generate branches, so the ECC hardware is genuinely absent from the disabled build.
  • In neorv32_cpu_control.vhd and neorv32_cpu_frontend.vhd, the SECDED/ parity component instances remain physically present in both configurations (this logic is fused too tightly into the FSM's combinational core to cleanly remove via generate without a larger restructuring); only their effect on execution and interrupt reporting is masked when HARDEN_EN is false.

TLS: program the FPGA through a secure connection¶

This example connects to the SK-RAFT server through TLS, reserves one device, uploads a bitstream and programs the FPGA. It does nothing else.

The connection uses authentication in the two directions:

  • The client verifies the server with the server certificate (server.crt).
  • The server accepts only a client that holds the private key (client.key) of the public key that you give to the server (client_public.pem).

The files¶

You make five files with OpenSSL. Each file has one location:

File Contents Location Used by
server.key Private key of the server Server only. Keep it secret. Server: -tls-key
server.crt Certificate of the server (public key of the server) Server and client Server: -tls-cert. Client: tls_server_cert
client.key Private key of the client Client only. Keep it secret. Client: tls_key
client.crt Certificate of the client (public key of the client) Client Client: tls_cert
client_public.pem Public key of the client Server Server: -tls-public-key

Make each private key on the computer that uses it. Then copy only the public files: server.crt to the client, and client_public.pem to the server.

Make the TLS files with OpenSSL (Linux)¶

Use OpenSSL 1.1.1 or a later version (openssl version). The commands make EC P-256 keys.

On the server computer¶

mkdir -p certs && cd certs

# 1. Private key of the server.
openssl genpkey -algorithm EC -pkeyopt ec_paramgen_curve:P-256 -out server.key
chmod 600 server.key

# 2. Self-signed certificate of the server, valid for 365 days.
#    Put in subjectAltName each address and host name that the clients use
#    to connect, for example the IP address of the server.
openssl req -new -x509 -key server.key -out server.crt -days 365 \
    -subj "/CN=sk-raft-server" \
    -addext "subjectAltName=IP:192.168.1.50,IP:127.0.0.1,DNS:localhost"

# 3. Examine the certificate: names and end date.
openssl x509 -in server.crt -noout -subject -ext subjectAltName -enddate

On the client computer¶

mkdir -p certs && cd certs

# 1. Private key of the client.
openssl genpkey -algorithm EC -pkeyopt ec_paramgen_curve:P-256 -out client.key
chmod 600 client.key

# 2. Self-signed certificate of the client. The server checks only the
#    public key in it, not the name or the dates.
openssl req -new -x509 -key client.key -out client.crt -days 365 \
    -subj "/CN=sk-raft-client"

# 3. Public key of the client, for the server.
openssl pkey -in client.key -pubout -out client_public.pem

# 4. Make sure that client.crt and client_public.pem hold the same key.
openssl x509 -in client.crt -noout -pubkey | diff - client_public.pem \
    && echo "public keys match"

Copy the public files¶

# From the client computer: the public key of the client to the server.
scp certs/client_public.pem user@192.168.1.50:sk-raft/certs/

# From the server computer: the certificate of the server to the client.
scp certs/server.crt user@client-host:sk-raft-client/application_examples/tls_program/certs/

To use RSA keys instead of EC keys, replace -algorithm EC -pkeyopt ec_paramgen_curve:P-256 with -algorithm RSA -pkeyopt rsa_keygen_bits:3072. The other commands do not change.

Start the server with TLS¶

Give the server the full paths of the TLS files. On Windows, the launcher runs the server in %LOCALAPPDATA%\SolidKosmos\sk-raft, not in the current folder. With a relative path, the server does not find the file and stops with failed to load TLS files: open certs\server.crt: The system cannot find the path specified.

On Windows, run the launcher from the folder of the server installation. The paths are an example:

bin\sk-raft.bat -port 50051 -tls-cert C:\sk-raft\certs\server.crt -tls-key C:\sk-raft\certs\server.key -tls-public-key C:\sk-raft\certs\client_public.pem

On Linux, give the same options to the server executable of the installation, for example with the files in ~/sk-raft/certs/:

<server executable> -port 50051 \
    -tls-cert ~/sk-raft/certs/server.crt -tls-key ~/sk-raft/certs/server.key \
    -tls-public-key ~/sk-raft/certs/client_public.pem

For the other options of the server, refer to the quick start in the README.

The server prints tls=true client-key=true. The server then refuses connections without TLS, and connections from clients that do not hold client.key. -tls-public-key also accepts client.crt, because the server uses only the public key in it.

How Python uses the files¶

gRPC in Python cannot load a bare public key. It uses certificates, which hold the public keys. Thus the client gives:

  • server.crt as the trusted root (root_certificates), to verify the server. The address in connect() must be in the subjectAltName of server.crt.
  • client.crt (certificate_chain) and client.key (private_key), to prove to the server that the client holds the private key of client_public.pem.

With the skraft package:

from skraft import SkraftFpga

client = SkraftFpga.connect(
    ip="192.168.1.50", port=50051,
    tls_server_cert="certs/server.crt",   # verify the server
    tls_cert="certs/client.crt",          # public key of the client
    tls_key="certs/client.key",           # private key of the client
)

SkraftFpga.connect() calls gRPC as shown below. Use this form only if you do not use the skraft package:

import grpc

def read(path):
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        return f.read()

credentials = grpc.ssl_channel_credentials(
    root_certificates=read("certs/server.crt"),
    private_key=read("certs/client.key"),
    certificate_chain=read("certs/client.crt"),
)
channel = grpc.secure_channel("192.168.1.50:50051", credentials)

Requirements¶

  • SK-RAFT server, with the FPGA board connected through JTAG.
  • Python 3.9 or a later version, with the skraft package installed (api/python).
  • The TLS files above, in certs/ next to src/. The .gitignore of this folder keeps certs/ out of Git.
  • A bitstream. By default, the script uses the prebuilt targeted_top design of the getting-started examples. Extract design_examples.zip first (see get_started/README.md).

Run the example¶

  1. At the top of src/main.py, set SK_RAFT_SERVER_IP, SERIAL_NUMBER and BOARD (or BITSTREAM).
  2. Run the script from src/:
cd src
python main.py

The script prints programmed <serial number> (<part number>) with <bitstream>. Then it releases the device and closes the connection.

The server serves only one client. The first client that sends a request becomes the client of the server. While it is connected, the requests of all other clients fail with the server serves only one client and another client is connected.

When the client disconnects, the server closes the device and the session itself. This also occurs if the connection stops before the script releases the device, for example when you press Ctrl+C. The server waits until the running requests of the client end, for example a programming request. Then the next client can connect.

Troubleshooting¶

If connect() raises ConnectionFailedError, do these checks:

  1. The server runs, with -tls-cert and -tls-key, on the port that you set.
  2. SK_RAFT_SERVER_IP is in the subjectAltName of server.crt (openssl x509 -in server.crt -noout -ext subjectAltName).
  3. server.crt on the client is the file that the server uses, and it did not expire (-enddate).
  4. client.crt holds the public key that the server got with -tls-public-key (step 4 on the client computer).
  5. No other client is connected to the server. If one is, the error says another client is connected.

To test the TLS connection without Python, use openssl s_client from the client computer:

openssl s_client -connect 192.168.1.50:50051 -alpn h2 -tls1_2 \
    -CAfile certs/server.crt -verify_return_error -verify_ip 192.168.1.50 \
    -cert certs/client.crt -key certs/client.key -brief </dev/null
  • Correct files: the output shows CONNECTION ESTABLISHED and Verification: OK.
  • certificate verify failed: the client refuses the server (checks 2 and 3).
  • alert bad certificate: the server refuses the client key (check 4).

The command uses TLS 1.2 (-tls1_2), because with TLS 1.3 the server refuses a client key only after s_client shows the connection.

XADC alarm: set off and clear the temperature alarm through JTAG¶

This example sets off and clears the temperature alarm (ALM0) of the XADC. The script moves the thresholds of the alarm around the temperature of the FPGA, and shows the state of the alarm. The temperature does not change: only the thresholds move.

The example has five stages. Each stage waits for Enter. During a stage, the script reads the temperature, the thresholds and the alarm twice per second, and writes the line again in place:

Device: serial number 210183BFD452A, part number XC7A35T
Original values: CONFIG0 = 0000h, CONFIG1 = 0000h, lower = -273.1C, upper = -273.1C
Temperature at the start: 46.4C. The thresholds move around this value.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Stage 1 of 5: both thresholds are above the temperature. ALM0 is off.
Press Enter for the next stage.
Temp =   46.5C | lower =   51.4C | upper =   56.4C | ALM0 = off

Stage 2 of 5: the temperature is between the thresholds. ALM0 stays off.
Press Enter for the next stage.
Temp =   46.4C | lower =   41.4C | upper =   51.4C | ALM0 = off

Stage 3 of 5: the temperature is above the upper threshold. ALM0 goes on.
Press Enter for the next stage.
Temp =   46.5C | lower =   36.4C | upper =   41.4C | ALM0 = ON

The values above are an example. The values of your device and board are different.

The script gives the thresholds in degrees Celsius. The SK-RAFT server converts them into the values of the alarm registers, with the transfer function of the family of the device, and decodes the state of the alarms from the flag register. The server accesses the XADC through the JTAG interface (the XADC_DRP instruction). The example does not need a design, and it does not program the FPGA.

How the temperature alarm works¶

ALM0 has hysteresis. Two thresholds control it:

Temperature ALM0
Above the upper threshold (TEMPERATURE_UPPER, alarm register 50h) Goes on.
Below the lower threshold (TEMPERATURE_LOWER, alarm register 54h) Goes off.
Between the two thresholds Does not change.

The XADC is in the default mode of the sequencer after power-up, and when the design does not use the XADC. In the default mode, the XADC disables all the alarms, except the over-temperature alarm (OT) (UG480 and UG580, Sequencer Modes). Thus the script sets the XADC to the single channel mode, on the temperature sensor. In this mode, the XADC converts only the temperature, and the alarms operate. The other sensors keep their last values until the end of the example.

The single channel mode is available in the XADC of the 7 series devices (UG480) and in the SYSMON of the UltraScale and UltraScale+ devices (UG580), with the same register values. Thus the same script operates on all these devices.

What the script does¶

  1. It reads the original values of CONFIG0, CONFIG1 and of the two thresholds, and the temperature at the start (T).
  2. It sets the thresholds of stage 1. Then it writes CONFIG0 and CONFIG1 to set the single channel mode, on the temperature sensor.
  3. It moves the thresholds for each stage, and shows the state of ALM0:
Stage Lower threshold Upper threshold ALM0
1 T + 5C T + 10C Off
2 T - 5C T + 5C Stays off
3 T - 10C T - 5C Goes on
4 T - 5C T + 5C Stays on
5 T + 5C T + 10C Goes off

Stages 2 and 4 use the same thresholds, but ALM0 is different: the state of ALM0 depends on the earlier stage. This is the hysteresis. Stage 1 puts ALM0 off, also if the alarm was on before the example.

  1. It writes back the original values: CONFIG1 first, then CONFIG0 and the two thresholds. The script also does this step when you press Ctrl+C, or when an error occurs.

The calls of the example¶

Call Use in the example
dev.xadc_alarm(TEMPERATURE_UPPER), dev.xadc_alarm(TEMPERATURE_LOWER) Read a threshold, in degrees Celsius.
dev.set_xadc_alarm(TEMPERATURE_UPPER, value), dev.set_xadc_alarm(TEMPERATURE_LOWER, value) Set a threshold, in degrees Celsius. The server converts the value, writes the alarm register and reads it back.
dev.xadc_flags() Read the state of the alarms: temperature is ALM0. jtag_read_only shows if the design allows only reads through JTAG.
dev.xadc(TEMPERATURE) Read the temperature, in degrees Celsius.
dev.read_xadc_register(XadcRegister.CONFIG0), dev.write_xadc_register(XadcRegister.CONFIG0, value) Read and write the channel of the single channel mode, as a raw 16-bit value.
dev.read_xadc_register(XadcRegister.CONFIG1), dev.write_xadc_register(XadcRegister.CONFIG1, value) Read and write the mode of the sequencer, as a raw 16-bit value.

During the example, CONFIG0 is 1000h:

Bits Name Value Meaning
13-12 AVG1-AVG0 01 Average of 16 samples, as in the default mode.
5-0 CH5-CH0 000000 The on-chip temperature sensor.

During the example, CONFIG1 is 3FDCh:

Bits Name Value Meaning
15-12 SEQ3-SEQ0 0011 Single channel mode (sequencer off).
11-8 ALM6-ALM3 1111 The VCCBRAM alarm and the alarms of the PS supplies are disabled.
7-4 CAL3-CAL0 1101 Correction of the ADC offset and of the supply sensors. CAL1 is 0, because the UltraScale SYSMON does not support it.
3-2 ALM2-ALM1 11 The VCCAUX and VCCINT alarms are disabled.
1 ALM0 0 The temperature alarm is enabled.
0 OT 0 The over-temperature alarm is enabled, as in the default mode.

Supported devices¶

Family Monitor Temperature transfer function Boards, for example
7 series, Zynq-7000 XADC (UG480) 503.975 / 273.15 Basys 3 (XC7A35T), ZedBoard (XC7Z020)
UltraScale SYSMONE1 (UG580) 501.3743 / 273.6777 (on-chip reference)
UltraScale+, Zynq UltraScale+ SYSMONE4 (UG580) 509.3140064 / 280.2308787 (internal reference) ZUBoard 1CG (XCZU1CG)

The script is the same for all these devices. The server selects the temperature transfer function by the family of the device. The server refuses the devices of other families, for example Versal devices.

Requirements¶

  • SK-RAFT server, with the FPGA board connected through JTAG. The server must support the XADC alarms (FpgaXadcAlarm, FpgaXadcSetAlarm and FpgaXadcFlags).
  • A 7 series, UltraScale or UltraScale+ device, for example one of the boards above.
  • Python 3.9 or a later version, with the skraft package installed (api/python).
  • A terminal that supports ANSI escape sequences, for example Windows Terminal, the Windows 10/11 console, or a Linux or macOS terminal.
  • No design files. The example does not upload or program a bitstream.

Run the example¶

  1. At the top of src/main.py, set SK_RAFT_SERVER_IP and SERIAL_NUMBER.
  2. Run the script:
cd src
python main.py
  1. Press Enter to go to the next stage. After stage 5, press Enter to stop.
Constant Default Description
SK_RAFT_SERVER_IP / SK_RAFT_SERVER_PORT "127.0.0.1" / 50051 The address of the SK-RAFT server.
SERIAL_NUMBER "210183BFD452A" The serial number of the target board. get_devices() gives the connected boards.
MARGIN_C 5.0 The distance between the thresholds and the temperature at the start, in degrees Celsius. The temperature must change by less than this value during the example.
READ_PERIOD_S 0.5 The time between two reads, in seconds.

Result¶

At the end, the script writes back the original values of CONFIG0, CONFIG1 and of the two thresholds. The XADC goes back to its original mode, for example the default mode, and all the sensors update again. If the script cannot write back the values (for example, if the connection to the server stops), switch the board off and on, or program the FPGA again.

While the example runs, a design that uses the XADC sees the changes: only the temperature updates, and the alarm outputs (ALM and OT) change. Thus run the example with a design that does not use the XADC, or with no design.

Use the alarms in your own script¶

from skraft import SkraftFpga, TEMPERATURE_UPPER, VCCINT_LOWER

with SkraftFpga.connect(ip="127.0.0.1", port=50051) as client:
    with client.attach("210183BFD452A") as dev:
        print(dev.xadc_alarm(TEMPERATURE_UPPER).value)  # degrees Celsius
        dev.set_xadc_alarm(TEMPERATURE_UPPER, 85.0)     # degrees Celsius
        dev.set_xadc_alarm(VCCINT_LOWER, 0.97)          # volts
        flags = dev.xadc_flags()
        print("ALM0 is on" if flags.temperature else "ALM0 is off")

dev.xadc_alarm() returns an XadcAlarm with two attributes: addr, the DRP address of the alarm register, and value, the threshold in SI units. dev.set_xadc_alarm() sets a threshold in SI units. Both functions accept a selector of the skraft library, or the DRP address of the alarm register:

Selectors (upper, lower) Alarm registers Unit Devices
TEMPERATURE_UPPER, TEMPERATURE_LOWER 50h, 54h degC All
OT_LIMIT, OT_RESET 53h, 57h degC All
VCCINT_UPPER, VCCINT_LOWER 51h, 55h V All
VCCAUX_UPPER, VCCAUX_LOWER 52h, 56h V All
VCCBRAM_UPPER, VCCBRAM_LOWER 58h, 5Ch V All
VCCPINT_UPPER, VCCPINT_LOWER 59h, 5Dh V Zynq-7000 only
VCCPAUX_UPPER, VCCPAUX_LOWER 5Ah, 5Eh V Zynq-7000 only
VCCO_DDR_UPPER, VCCO_DDR_LOWER 5Bh, 5Fh V Zynq-7000 only

The server converts the thresholds with the transfer functions of UG480 and UG580, the same functions as dev.xadc(). For the temperatures, it uses the transfer function of the family of the device (see Supported devices). It keeps the four least significant bits of the alarm register, and reads the register back after the write. A threshold outside the range of the ADC (for example, -273.15 to 230.70 degC and 0 to 2.9993 V for the 7 series) causes an error that gives the range.

dev.xadc_flags() returns an XadcFlags. The attributes temperature, vccint, vccaux, over_temperature, vccbram, vccpint, vccpaux and vcco_ddr are True while the alarm is on. The attributes internal_reference, jtag_read_only and jtag_disabled show the reference of the ADC and the JTAG access that the design allows. The flag register (3Fh) has the same bits in the XADC and in the SYSMON.

If a read or a write fails, the functions raise XadcError.

Caution: the four least significant bits of the OT_LIMIT register (53h) control the over-temperature limit. In 7 series devices, the value 0011b enables the automatic shutdown, if the bitstream also enables it (BITSTREAM.CONFIG.OVERTEMPPOWERDOWN). If the register holds 0000h, the limit is 125 degC. In UltraScale and UltraScale+ devices, the value 0011b enables the limit of OT_LIMIT, else the limit is 125 degC. The automatic shutdown needs BITSTREAM.CONFIG.OVERTEMPSHUTDOWN. When the automatic shutdown is enabled, the device shuts down when the temperature is above the limit. dev.set_xadc_alarm() does not change these four bits.

Troubleshooting¶

Problem Cause Solution
the XADC of the ... family is not supported The device does not have an XADC or a SYSMON that the server supports, for example a Versal device. Use a 7 series, UltraScale or UltraScale+ device.
The design allows only reads of the XADC through JTAG (JTAG_XADC = StatusOnly). The design sets BITSTREAM.GENERAL.JTAG_XADC (or JTAG_SYSMON) to StatusOnly. Program the FPGA with a design that does not limit the JTAG access to the XADC.
XADC alarm 50h holds ...h after the write of ...h, the design may limit the JTAG access to the XADC The XADC ignores the writes through JTAG. A possible cause: the design disables the JTAG access to the XADC (JTAG_XADC or JTAG_SYSMON is Disable), or the PS of a Zynq-7000 device uses the XADC through its dedicated interface. Program the FPGA with a design that does not disable the JTAG access.
failed to read the XADC flags: unknown method FpgaXadcFlags ... The SK-RAFT server is older than the client, and does not support the XADC alarms. Update the SK-RAFT server.
ALM0 goes off in stage 4 (UltraScale+ devices) Bit 0 of the lower temperature register (54h) is 1: the temperature alarm operates in the window mode, not in the hysteresis mode (UG580, Thermal Management). The server keeps this bit. Use a design that keeps the hysteresis mode (bit 0 of INIT_54 is 0), or no design.
ALM0 does not go on in stage 3 The design uses the XADC, and changes CONFIG0, CONFIG1 or the thresholds through the DRP of the XADC. Run the example with a design that does not use the XADC, or with no design.
The line shows ←[K, or a new line appears at each read The terminal does not support ANSI escape sequences (for example, some IDE consoles). Run the script in a terminal window.

XADC monitor: temperature and voltages through JTAG¶

This example reads the temperature and voltage sensors of the FPGA once per second. Each sensor has one line, with its current value and its highest and lowest values. The script writes the lines again after each read, so the values update in place:

Device: serial number 210183BFD452A, part number XC7A35T
Reading the XADC once per second. Press Enter to stop.
max/min: the highest and lowest values since power-up or the last XADC reset.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Temp  =   46.4C | max=  47.2C | min=  30.1C
vint  =   999mV | max= 1003mV | min=  997mV
vaux  =  1799mV | max= 1802mV | min= 1796mV
vbram =  1000mV | max= 1002mV | min=  998mV

The values above are an example. The values of your device and board are different. The first line shows the serial number of the JTAG cable and the part number of the device that the SK-RAFT server selected.

The SK-RAFT server reads the sensors through the JTAG interface (the XADC_DRP instruction). The example does not need a design, and it does not program the FPGA. If the FPGA is not configured, or the design does not use the sensors, the device monitors its on-chip sensors by itself.

Supported devices¶

The folder has one script for each board:

Script Board Device Family PS supplies
src/main_basys3.py Basys 3 XC7A35T 7 series No
src/main_zedboard.py ZedBoard XC7Z020 Zynq-7000 Yes (vpint, vpaux, vddr)
src/main_zuboard_1cg.py ZUBoard 1CG XCZU1CG Zynq UltraScale+ No

The scripts are the same, except for the ZYNQ setting. src/main_basys3.py also works with other 7 series boards. For another Zynq-7000 board, use src/main_zedboard.py.

In 7 series and Zynq-7000 devices, the sensors are in the XADC (UG480). In Zynq UltraScale+ devices, they are in the System Monitor, SYSMON (UG580). The skraft library and the scripts call both of them XADC.

What the example reads¶

Label Sensor Selectors (value, max, min) Status registers Unit Devices
Temp Die temperature TEMPERATURE, MAX_TEMPERATURE, MIN_TEMPERATURE 00h, 20h, 24h C All
vint Internal core supply VCCINT, MAX_VCCINT, MIN_VCCINT 01h, 21h, 25h mV All
vaux Auxiliary supply VCCAUX, MAX_VCCAUX, MIN_VCCAUX 02h, 22h, 26h mV All
vbram Block RAM supply VCCBRAM, MAX_VCCBRAM, MIN_VCCBRAM 06h, 23h, 27h mV All
vpint PS internal supply VCCPINT, MAX_VCCPINT, MIN_VCCPINT 0Dh, 28h, 2Ch mV Zynq-7000 only
vpaux PS auxiliary supply VCCPAUX, MAX_VCCPAUX, MIN_VCCPAUX 0Eh, 29h, 2Dh mV Zynq-7000 only
vddr PS DDR I/O supply VCCO_DDR, MAX_VCCO_DDR, MIN_VCCO_DDR 0Fh, 2Ah, 2Eh mV Zynq-7000 only

max and min are the highest and the lowest values since power-up or the last XADC reset.

Requirements¶

  • SK-RAFT server, with the FPGA board connected through JTAG.
  • A 7 series FPGA, a Zynq-7000 device or a Zynq UltraScale+ device, for example one of the boards above.
  • Python 3.9 or a later version, with the skraft package installed (api/python).
  • A terminal that supports ANSI escape sequences, for example Windows Terminal, the Windows 10/11 console, or a Linux or macOS terminal.
  • No design files. The example does not upload or program a bitstream.

Run the example¶

  1. At the top of the script for your board, set SK_RAFT_SERVER_IP and SERIAL_NUMBER.
  2. Run the script for your board:
cd src
python main_basys3.py        # Basys 3, or another 7 series board
python main_zedboard.py      # ZedBoard
python main_zuboard_1cg.py   # ZUBoard 1CG
  1. Press Enter to stop.
Constant Default Description
SK_RAFT_SERVER_IP / SK_RAFT_SERVER_PORT "127.0.0.1" / 50051 The address of the SK-RAFT server.
SERIAL_NUMBER "210183BFD452A" The serial number of the target board. get_devices() gives the connected boards.
ZYNQ True in main_zedboard.py, False in the other scripts True adds the PS supplies (vpint, vpaux, vddr). Set it only for a Zynq-7000 device. The server reads these sensors only in Zynq-7000 devices: on other devices, the script stops with an error.
READ_PERIOD_S 1.0 The time between two reads, in seconds.

Result¶

The script only reads the sensors. It does not change the configuration of the FPGA. Thus you can run it before or after the other examples, with no reprogramming.

Read the XADC in your own script¶

from skraft import SkraftFpga, TEMPERATURE, VCCINT, MAX_VCCINT

with SkraftFpga.connect(ip="127.0.0.1", port=50051) as client:
    with client.attach("210183BFD452A") as dev:
        print(dev.serial_number, dev.part_number)
        print(dev.xadc(TEMPERATURE).value)  # degrees Celsius
        print(dev.xadc(VCCINT).value)       # volts
        print(dev.xadc(MAX_VCCINT).value)   # volts, highest since power-up
        print(dev.xadc(0x01).value)         # volts: VCCINT, by its DRP address

client.attach() returns the device with its serial number and its part number. dev.xadc() accepts a selector of the skraft library, or the DRP address of a status register (UG480, UG580). It returns an XadcSensor with two attributes:

  • addr: the DRP address that the server read.
  • value: the value, in SI units. Degrees Celsius for temperatures, volts for voltages.

The library has a selector for each sensor in the table above. It also has VREFP and VREFN, the voltages on the reference inputs of the ADC. On a board that uses the on-chip reference, these pins connect to ground, and both values are 0 V. Thus the example does not show them.

dev.xadc() reads only the on-chip sensors. It does not read the external analog inputs (VP/VN and VAUX), the calibration registers or the flag register. For the alarms and the flag register, use dev.xadc_alarm(), dev.set_xadc_alarm() and dev.xadc_flags(): see the xadc_alarm example. If a read fails, dev.xadc() raises XadcError. XadcError is a SkraftError.

Troubleshooting¶

Problem Cause Solution
XADC sensor 0Dh is available only in Zynq-7000 SoCs, not in ... ZYNQ = True, but the device is not a Zynq-7000 device. Set ZYNQ = False, or use the script for your board.
DRP address ...h is not an XADC sensor Your script gives a DRP address that is not a supported sensor. Use a selector, or an address from the table above.
Temp is approximately -273C and all voltages are 0mV The device returned only zeros. A possible cause: the design on the FPGA disables the JTAG access to the sensors (BITSTREAM.GENERAL.JTAG_XADC on 7 series and Zynq-7000 devices). Program the FPGA with a design that does not disable the JTAG access.
The part number is empty The SK-RAFT server is older than the client, and does not send the part number. Update the SK-RAFT server.
A new block of lines appears each second The terminal does not support ANSI escape sequences (for example, some IDE consoles). Run the script in a terminal window.

Auxiliary components¶

Reusable building blocks for designs that are tested with SK-RAFT. Each one is independent and has its own README with the details.

Component What it does Why you need it
bscan/ VHDL for up to four JTAG USER registers (USER1 to USER4) through the BSCANE2 primitive, with a read path and a write path. Lets the SK-RAFT client talk to your design over the same JTAG cable it uses for injection: set inputs, read results, control the clock. No UART or extra pins.
safe_clk_gen/ clk_gen_wrapper: a PLL that makes the design clock (any output frequency) and keeps it off until the PLL has locked. 7-series, UltraScale and UltraScale+. A clean design clock that starts without glitches. It is the clock that a BSCAN-controlled clock gate (BUFGCE) stops during an injection.
bram_hold_pass/ A Vivado Tcl netlist pass that adds a hold register behind every block RAM output without an output register. An SK-RAFT access to BRAM content frames (readback, inject, revert) overwrites the BRAM output latch. Without the hold register, the design reads that wrong value after the clock resumes.

How they fit together¶

A typical fault-injection setup with SK-RAFT stops the design, changes the configuration memory, and starts the design again:

  1. safe_clk_gen makes the design clock.
  2. A BUFGCE gates that clock. Its enable comes from a bscan USER register (for example USER1), so the SK-RAFT client can stop and start the design with write_bscan.
  3. With the clock stopped, the client injects (and reverts) bits.
  4. The client starts the clock again and reads the result through other bscan USER registers.
  5. bram_hold_pass makes sure that step 3 does not change the words the design read from its block RAMs before the freeze.

The bscan README shows the clock gate (USER1 + BUFGCE) in VHDL, with the XDC lines and the Python calls.

Used in¶

  • get_started/ (the getting-started examples): BSCAN registers, safe clock, and the hold pass for brams_top (example 4).
  • application_examples/test_neo_hardened/ (NEORV32): BSCAN registers, safe clock, and the hold pass.
  • application_examples/sem_arbitration/ (SEM IP, Basys 3 and TE0841): BSCAN registers and safe clock.
  • application_examples/mmcm_drp_interface/ (MMCM reconfiguration through the DRP): BSCAN registers and safe clock.

The examples do not keep copies of these VHDL files. Their create_project.tcl scripts add the files from this folder.

BRAM hold register pass (7-series and UltraScale)¶

The problem¶

SK-RAFT reads and writes the BRAM content through the configuration interface (readback, inject and revert). Each access to a BRAM content frame changes the output latch of the BRAMs in that frame. The value on Data Output port (DO) changes. The stored content and the FIFO pointers do not change.

A design reads the latch each time it uses DO after the read cycle. If a freeze, an injection and a resume occur between the read and that use, the design gets the changed value. It does not get the word that it read.

This problem occurs only on ports without the output register (DO_REG = 0). With DOA_REG, DOB_REG or DO_REG = 1, the output register keeps the word while the clock is stopped. These ports do not need the pass.

The fix: a hold register¶

A hold register is a flip-flop on the opposite clock edge of the BRAM read clock. It copies DO in the half cycle after each read. All the logic that used DO uses the hold register instead.

-- BRAM on rising_edge(clk), DO_REG = 0
process (clk) begin                       -- read enable, registered
  if rising_edge(clk) then ren_d <= bram_en; end if;
end process;
process (clk) begin                       -- hold register
  if falling_edge(clk) then
    if ren_d = '1' then hold <= bram_do; end if;
  end if;
end process;
-- the design uses hold, not bram_do

The hold register must load only directly after a read. Its clock enable (CE) is the registered read enable. A falling-edge register that loads on each cycle is not a hold register: after the resume, it loads the changed latch.

bram_hold_pass.tcl adds this structure to the netlist. You do not change the source.

Requirements on the design¶

  1. The clock must stop after an edge of the hold register. Between the last read edge and the freeze, an edge of the hold register must occur. For a BRAM on the rising edge, gate the clock with a buffer that stops low: BUFGCE, or BUFGCTRL with INIT_OUT = 0. Do not use BUFGCE_1. For a BRAM with an inverted clock (IS_CLK*_INVERTED = 1), do the opposite. The pass gives a warning if a gating buffer stops on the wrong level.
  2. You are responsible for the timing of the half-cycle paths. The path from the BRAM to the hold register gets half a clock period. The path from the hold register to its loads also gets half a clock period. The pass adds no constraints, and Vivado times these paths normally. If they fail, decrease the clock frequency or use DO_REG = 1 on that port.
  3. Inject only while the clock is stopped. The hold register keeps the word that the design read before the freeze. It does not make an access to a BRAM safe while the clock runs.
  4. Exclude the BRAMs from power optimization. Add this line to the XDC:
set_power_opt -exclude_cells [get_cells -hier -filter {REF_NAME =~ RAMB*}]

This prevents the tool from changing how the BRAMs do their reads. Without this line, the power optimization of opt_design runs after the pass and can add gating logic to a read enable, also to a read enable that is tied to 1. Then the BRAM reads less frequently than the pass expects. The XDC files of the examples in this repository have this line.

What the pass does¶

The pass examines each BRAM read port of these primitives: RAMB18E1, RAMB36E1, FIFO18E1 and FIFO36E1 (7-series), and RAMB18E2, RAMB36E2, FIFO18E2 and FIFO36E2 (UltraScale).

Case Action
DO_REG = 1. This includes all asynchronous and FWFT 7-series FIFOs, and the UltraScale FIFOs with REGISTER_MODE other than UNREGISTERED. Skipped
No output pin of the port has a load. Skipped
The port enable is tied to 0. Skipped
Each load is already a hold register (opposite edge, CE = the read enable registered on the BRAM edge). Skipped
The loads are opposite-edge flip-flops with a different CE. Protected (see below) and reported
64K x 1 cascade (RAM_EXTENSION). Hold register on the UPPER output. Its enable includes both halves. The LOWER output has no loads and is skipped.
All other ports with DO_REG = 0. Hold register added
UltraScale RAMB*E2 with full-width read (READ_WIDTH_A = 72 or 36). One read port on port A: DOUTADOUT, DOUTBDOUT, the parity outputs and the ECC outputs
Other UltraScale RAMB*E2. Ports A and B separately (DOUTADOUT and DOUTBDOUT)
UltraScale cascades (CASCADE_ORDER other than NONE), FWFT FIFO*E2 without the output register, and URAM. Reported, not changed
  • The pass connects each load according to the clock edge on which the load samples the word. A load can be a register, or logic that goes to registers.
Load samples on Connected to Reason
The BRAM edge The hold register The hold register has the word half a cycle before the load samples it. The timing does not change.
The opposite edge A multiplexer (one LUT3 for each bit). It selects DO in the half cycle after a read, and the hold register at all other times. The hold register loads on the same edge as the load, so a load behind it gets the word one cycle late. The multiplexer gives the load DO directly after a read, as before.
No clock edge (for example an output port) The hold register
Both edges (logic that goes to registers on both edges) The multiplexer, with a warning The pass cannot split the logic. A register on the BRAM edge behind this logic is not protected if a read occurs on the last edge before a freeze. Correct this logic manually.

If the port enable is tied to 1, the opposite-edge loads stay on DO. The port reads on each cycle, so a new word replaces the changed latch before these loads sample it. This is correct only with requirement 4. - Only output pins with loads get a hold flip-flop. - The CE of the hold register is the OR of the port enable and the output latch reset (RAMB18E1 and RAMB36E1), registered on the BRAM edge. Ports with the same clock and the same enable signals share one enable flip-flop. If the enable is tied to 1, the pass adds no enable flip-flop. - The pass uses the IS_*_INVERTED properties of the BRAM clock, enable and reset pins. - All the cells that the pass adds have DONT_TOUCH. - The pass does not add hold registers to the FIFO flags (EMPTY, FULL and the other flags). The flags do not come from the output latch.

Running it¶

In a project, set the pass as the hook before opt_design. Do this before you start impl_1:

set_property STEPS.OPT_DESIGN.TCL.PRE \
    /path/to/auxiliary_components/bram_hold_pass/bram_hold_hook.tcl \
    [get_runs impl_1]

The examples do this in their create_project.tcl files: get_started/hw/create_project.tcl (for brams_top) and application_examples/test_neo_hardened/create_project.tcl.

The pass writes its report to bram_hold_pass.rpt in the impl_1 run directory. To give options, copy bram_hold_hook.tcl and add the options to the bram_hold::run line.

In a non-project flow, run the pass after synth_design or link_design:

source bram_hold_pass.tcl
bram_hold::run

Options:

Option Effect
-dry_run Writes the report only. Changes nothing.
-report file The name of the report file. The default is bram_hold_pass.rpt.
-exclude {pattern ...} Does not change the BRAM cells whose names match a pattern (glob).
-trust_existing Accepts each opposite-edge flip-flop as a hold register. The pass does not examine its CE.

Use -exclude for BRAMs that you protect yourself. Use -trust_existing only if you know that your opposite-edge registers load only after reads.

Reading the report¶

The header gives the number of ports and cells for each decision. Then the report has one line for each BRAM:

  • held N pins: the pass added N hold flip-flops.
  • (K of these pins feed only opposite-edge flip-flops that are not hold registers ...): the CE of these registers is not the registered read enable. The pass protected them.
  • (K opposite-edge loads get DO in the half cycle after a read, the hold otherwise): K loads are connected through the multiplexer.
  • WARNING: K loads reach registers on both clock edges: refer to the table above, and examine this logic manually.
  • already held: the source already has the hold structure.
  • DO_REG = 1, no loads, port never enabled, excluded: the pass skipped the port.
  • WARNING: clock buffer ... stops on the wrong level: correct the clock gating (requirement 1). If you do not, the hold register does not protect a read on the last edge before a freeze.
  • ERROR: the pass cannot process the cell (for example, a protected IP). The cell does not change.

Known limits¶

  • Built-in ECC (EN_ECC_WRITE = TRUE): the hold register also keeps the ECC outputs. But an SK-RAFT injection into such a BRAM never causes an ECC error. When SK-RAFT writes the frame, the ECC encoder of the BRAM calculates new ECC bits for the changed data. Thus the stored word is a valid ECC word, and the flipped bit is silent data corruption. The ECC does not detect or correct it.
  • UltraScale: the pass supports RAMBE2 and FIFOE2. The latch behaviour is the same as on 7-series. The pass reports RAMBE2 output cascades (CASCADE_ORDER, CASDOMUX), FWFT FIFOE2 without the output register, and URAM, but does not change them.
  • Latch reset in FIFOs: the CE of a FIFO hold register is the registered RDEN.

BSCAN USER registers¶

VHDL that gives a design up to four registers on the JTAG chain of the FPGA (USER1 to USER4), through the BSCANE2 primitive. The SK-RAFT client reads and writes them with read_bscan and write_bscan, over the same JTAG cable it uses for fault injection.

Works on 7-series, UltraScale and UltraScale+ (BSCANE2 exists in all of them).

Files¶

File Contents
bscan_interface.vhd The component to instantiate: one USER register with a write path (JTAG to design) and a read path (design to JTAG). Uses the two files below.
bscan_primitive_wrapper.vhd The BSCANE2 instance for one USER chain.
bscan_user_register_io.vhd The shift registers and the small FSM that tells a read from a write.

Add all three files to the project. bscan_interface instantiates the other two with entity work.…, so no package is needed.

bscan_interface¶

generic (
  jtag_chain : integer range 1 to 4;  -- 1 = USER1 ... 4 = USER4
  data_len_r : positive;              -- bits read by JTAG (design to JTAG)
  data_len_w : positive;              -- bits written by JTAG (JTAG to design)
  sync       : boolean := true        -- synchronize avail/ack to clk_i
);
port (
  clk_i            : in  std_ulogic;  -- design clock (for sync = true)
  tck_o, drck_o    : out std_ulogic;  -- TCK and DRCK, if you need them
  data_to_jtag_i   : in  std_ulogic_vector(data_len_r - 1 downto 0);
  data_from_jtag_o : out std_ulogic_vector(data_len_w - 1 downto 0);
  ux_avail_o       : out std_ulogic;  -- 1 after a write, until the next shift
  ux_ack_o         : out std_ulogic   -- one-cycle strobe when a read captures
);

One instance per USER chain. Each chain (1 to 4) can be used once in a design.

How a read and a write work¶

JTAG shifts the register LSB first. What happens at the end of the shift decides between a read and a write:

  • Write (write_bscan): Shift-DR, Exit1-DR, Update-DR. At Update-DR the shifted value goes to data_from_jtag_o and ux_avail_o goes to 1. ux_avail_o goes back to 0 when the next shift starts.
  • Read (read_bscan): at Capture-DR the register loads data_to_jtag_i (ux_ack_o pulses), then shifts it out on TDO. The path ends through Pause-DR, not Update-DR, so data_from_jtag_o does not change: a read never writes.

Clock domain crossing¶

The register runs on TCK (about 15 MHz). The design runs on its own clock.

  • sync => true: two flip-flops synchronize ux_avail_o and ux_ack_o to clk_i (with ASYNC_REG).
  • The data path is not synchronized. data_from_jtag_o changes only at Update-DR, so take it on the rising edge of the synchronized ux_avail_o; it is stable by then:
process (clk)
begin
  if rising_edge(clk) then
    avail_prev <= avail;
    if avail = '1' and avail_prev = '0' then   -- one new write
      value <= data_from_jtag;
    end if;
  end if;
end process;
  • data_to_jtag_i is captured on TCK at Capture-DR. Keep it stable while a read can happen (for example a register that changes only when the design writes it).
  • sync => false with clk_i => '0': for a register that is not tied to a design clock, for example the clock enable below.

Example: clock gate on USER1¶

USER1 stops and starts the design clock. 1 = runs, 0 = stopped (0 after programming). safe_clk comes from safe_clk_gen.

signal gated_clk                    : std_ulogic;
signal clk_en_jtag, clk_en_rb       : std_ulogic_vector(0 downto 0);
signal clk_en_d0, clk_en_sync       : std_ulogic := '0';

bscan_u1_clk_en : entity work.bscan_interface
  generic map (jtag_chain => 1, data_len_r => 1, data_len_w => 1,
               sync => false)
  port map (clk_i => '0', tck_o => open, drck_o => open,
            data_to_jtag_i => clk_en_rb, data_from_jtag_o => clk_en_jtag,
            ux_avail_o => open, ux_ack_o => open);

process (safe_clk)                     -- two flip-flops: TCK to safe_clk
begin
  if rising_edge(safe_clk) then
    clk_en_d0   <= clk_en_jtag(0);
    clk_en_sync <= clk_en_d0;
  end if;
end process;
clk_en_rb(0) <= clk_en_sync;           -- USER1 reads back the enable

clk_gate : BUFGCE                      -- stops its output low
  port map (O => gated_clk, CE => clk_en_sync, I => safe_clk);

Clock all logic you want to freeze from gated_clk. Use a BUFGCE (stops low), not a BUFGCE_1, when the design has block RAMs protected by bram_hold_pass.

XDC: the TCK clock¶

bscan_interface puts TCK on a BUFG (tck_BUFG_inst). Declare it as a clock and make it asynchronous to the design clock, once per instance:

create_clock -period 66.667 -name bscan_clk_u1 -waveform {0.000 33.333} \
    [get_pins -filter REF_PIN_NAME==O -of_objects \
        [get_cells bscan_u1_clk_en/tck_BUFG_inst]]

set_clock_groups -asynchronous \
    -group [get_clocks -include_generated_clocks sys_clk_pin] \
    -group [get_clocks bscan_clk_u1]

sys_clk_pin is the board clock in your XDC; bscan_u1_clk_en is the instance name.

Python (SK-RAFT client)¶

from skraft import BscanPrimitive

USER_CLK_EN = BscanPrimitive(1, 1)     # USER1, 1 bit
USER_DATA = BscanPrimitive(3, 32)      # USER3, 32 bits

dev.write_bscan(USER_CLK_EN, 1)        # start the clock
dev.write_bscan(USER_DATA, 0x1234)     # write
value = int.from_bytes(dev.read_bscan(USER_DATA), "big")   # read

BscanPrimitive(chain, length) takes one length. Give data_len_r and data_len_w the same value for a register you both read and write.

Notes¶

  • Vivado debug cores (ILA, VIO) use a BSCANE2 for their debug hub, by default on USER1. Move the debug hub to a free chain (or do not use that chain here) if you use both.
  • A write is complete only after Update-DR. A read never changes the design side of the register.

Safe clock generator (clk_gen_wrapper)¶

A PLL that makes the design clock from the board clock, for 7-series, UltraScale and UltraScale+, and keeps the output off until the PLL is locked and stable ("safe startup").

What it does¶

  • Instantiates the native PLL of the family: PLLE2_BASE (7-series), PLLE3_BASE (UltraScale) or PLLE4_BASE (UltraScale+).
  • Calculates the PLL settings (DIVCLK_DIVIDE, CLKFBOUT_MULT, CLKOUT0_DIVIDE) at elaboration, inside the VCO and PFD ranges of the family, and picks the setting closest to the requested frequency. No Clocking Wizard IP is needed.
  • Sends LOCKED through an 8-stage shift register, and enables the output BUFGCE only after that. The design never sees the clock before the PLL is stable (the same behaviour as SAFE_STARTUP in the Clocking Wizard).

Interface¶

generic (
  g_family          : string := "7SERIES";  -- or "ULTRASCALE", "ULTRASCALEPLUS"
  g_clkin_period_ns : real   := 10.0;       -- input clock period
  g_clkout_freq_mhz : real   := 0.0         -- output frequency, 0.0 = same as input
);
port (
  clk_i    : in  std_ulogic;  -- board clock
  clk_o    : out std_ulogic;  -- design clock (on a BUFGCE)
  locked_o : out std_ulogic   -- 1 when clk_o runs
);

Usage¶

safe_clk_gen : entity work.clk_gen_wrapper
  generic map (
    g_family          => "7SERIES",
    g_clkin_period_ns => 10.0,     -- 100 MHz board clock
    g_clkout_freq_mhz => 70.0      -- 70 MHz design clock
  )
  port map (clk_i => clk_i, clk_o => safe_clk, locked_o => open);

At elaboration the wrapper reports the setting it chose (a note that starts with clk_gen_wrapper: family=; for 100 MHz in and 70 MHz out it is D=1, M=14, O=20, exactly 70 MHz). If the closest setting is more than 0.1 % from the request, it reports a warning with the real frequency. Use the real frequency in the rest of the design (for example a CPU clock frequency generic).

Constrain only the input clock in the XDC (create_clock on clk_i). Vivado derives the output clock from the PLL.

Using it with SK-RAFT¶

safe_clk is the clock that a BSCAN-controlled clock gate stops during an injection: safe_clk into a BUFGCE whose CE is a USER register. The bscan README has the VHDL, the XDC and the Python calls.

Notes¶

  • The VCO and PFD limits in the wrapper are for the slowest speed grade of each family. Check the PLL switching characteristics in the data sheet of your part if you need a setting at the edge of the range.
  • If no legal setting exists for the input clock, elaboration stops with an assertion that names the family and the input frequency.
  • The PLL has no reset input (RST tied low). It locks after configuration.

SK-RAFT Protocol Buffers definition¶

The skraft_client.proto file in this folder defines the full SK-RAFT gRPC API: its services, methods and messages.

You can use it to generate a client for SK-RAFT in any language that gRPC supports, such as C++, C#, Go, Java, Node.js or Python. For example, in Python:

pip install grpcio grpcio-tools
python -m grpc_tools.protoc -I . --python_out=. --grpc_python_out=. skraft_client.proto

For setup instructions and guides for other languages, see the gRPC documentation: https://grpc.io/docs/

Index

To install the client on a computer that has no internet access, make an offline bundle on a computer that has internet access:

python make_bundle.py --target linux-x86_64 --target windows-amd64 --python-version 3.11
  • --target is the platform of the computer without internet access: linux-x86_64, linux-aarch64 or windows-amd64. Repeat it for more platforms.
  • --python-version is the Python version of that computer. Repeat it for more versions. The bundle must have the correct version, because grpcio contains compiled code.
  • Without these options, the bundle is for the platform and the Python version that run the script.
  • To pin the versions of the dependencies, give a requirements file with --requirements.

You can also run bundler.sh on Linux or bundler.bat on Windows. Without options, these scripts make a bundle for linux-x86_64 and windows-amd64. They give other options to make_bundle.py, and they find a Python with pip for you.

The script writes an archive to api/python/dist. Copy the archive to the computer without internet access and extract it. Then run ./install.sh on Linux or install.bat on Windows. The installer does not use the network. It installs the client and pyserial, which some examples use, into the active virtual environment, or else into .venv in the current directory. For more options, run python install.py --help.

uploadDesignToServer(design) ¶

Upload the files of a design to the server.

Each file is sent in its own stream through the FpgaUploadDesignFile RPC. The server keeps the files of each design in a folder of its own. Thus, you can upload several designs, and then program one of them with programFPGA. Once every file has been sent, the design is also kept on the client so that later calls can check which files are available.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default
design Design

The design whose files should be uploaded. Files that are not set are skipped.

 required

Raises:

Type Description
DesignFileError

If a design file cannot be read or its upload fails.

programFPGA(design=None) ¶

Program the device with an uploaded design.

Upload the design with uploadDesignToServer first. The server keeps each uploaded design. Thus, you can upload several designs, and then program the one to use. The client reads the local files of the design again, and the server checks that its copies are the same. After the programming, later calls check the files of this design. Uses the FpgaProgram RPC.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default
design Optional[Design]

The design to program. If not given, the design that was last uploaded or programmed is used.

 None

Raises:

Type Description
TypeError

If the design is not a Design.
DesignFileError

If the design has no bitstream, or if a design file cannot be read.
ConnectionFailedError

If the server could not program the device, for example because the design was not uploaded.

Examples:

>>> dev.uploadDesignToServer(design_a)
>>> dev.uploadDesignToServer(design_b)
>>> dev.programFPGA(design_a)
>>> dev.programFPGA(design_b)

Examples:

>>> frames = dev.readback(ReadbackOption.READBACK)
>>> dev.write_frame(frames[1])

all_bit_counts(pblock=None) ¶

Get every bit count for the loaded design in one call.

Without a pblock, the counts cover the whole device and come from the FpgaGetAllBitCounts RPC. With a pblock, each count only includes the bits that fall inside that pblock, and each memory type is requested separately. A memory type whose design file has not been uploaded gives a count of 0.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default
pblock Optional[str]

The name of a pblock from the constraints (XDC) file. If omitted, the whole device is counted. Using a pblock requires the constraints file.

 None

Returns:

Type Description
dict[str, int]

dict[str, int]: The bit counts, under the keys cram_bits, essential_cram_bits, bram_bits, flip_flop_bits, lutram_bits, pblock_bits and pblock_essential_bits.

Raises:

Type Description
DesignFileError

If a pblock is given and the constraints (XDC) file has not been uploaded.
ConnectionFailedError

If the server could not provide the counts.

bit_count(target, pblock=None) ¶

Count the bits of one memory type in the loaded design.

CRAM counts every configuration bit. ESSENTIAL_CRAM counts the essential bits and needs the essential bits (EBD) file. FF, LUTRAM and BRAM count storage element bits and need the logic location (LL) file. Uses the FpgaGetBitCount RPC.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default
target TargetMemory

The memory type to count. Only one memory type can be given.

 required
pblock Optional[str]

The name of a pblock from the constraints (XDC) file. If given, only the bits inside that pblock are counted.

 None

Returns:

Name Type Description
int int

The number of bits.

Raises:

Type Description
DesignFileError

If a design file needed for the target or the pblock has not been uploaded.
ValueError

If the target is not a single memory type.
ConnectionFailedError

If the server could not count the bits.

configure_seed(seed) ¶

Set the seed of the random generator for random injections.

With the same seed, the same design and the same targets, inject_random selects the same sequence of locations. Thus, you can repeat a random campaign. Each SkraftFpga.attach sets a new seed from the current time. Thus, set the seed after attach. Uses the FpgaConfigureSeed RPC.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default
seed int

The seed, from 0 to 2**32 - 1.

 required

Raises:

Type Description
TypeError

If the seed is not an integer.
ValueError

If the seed is out of range.
ConnectionFailedError

If the server could not set the seed.

Examples:

>>> dev.configure_seed(42)
>>> dev.inject_random(TargetMemory.ESSENTIAL_CRAM)

configure_jtag_frequency(frequency) ¶

Set the JTAG clock (TCK) frequency of the FTDI that accesses the device.

The frequency is from 460 kHz to 15 MHz. The FTDI makes only the frequencies 30 MHz / n, for an integer n. Thus, use one of the JTAG_* constants, for example JTAG_10_MHZ, to get the frequency without change. See JtagFrequency. Uses the FpgaConfigureFrequency RPC.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default
frequency JtagFrequency

The TCK frequency.

 required

Raises:

Type Description
TypeError

If the frequency is not a JtagFrequency.
JtagError

If the server could not set the frequency.

Examples:

>>> dev.configure_jtag_frequency(JTAG_10_MHZ)
>>> dev.configure_jtag_frequency(
...     JtagFrequency(750, FrequencyUnit.KHZ)
... )

configure_latency(latency_ms) ¶

Set the latency timer of the FTDI that accesses the device.

The FTDI sends the data that it holds to the host when the latency timer expires, if its buffer is not full. Uses the FpgaConfigureLatency RPC.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default
latency_ms int

The latency, in milliseconds (ms), from 0 to 255. The FTDI driver can refuse low values.

 required

Raises:

TypeError

If the latency is not an integer.
ValueError

If the latency does not fit in 8 bits.
JtagError

If the server could not set the latency.

Examples:

>>> dev.configure_latency(2)

inject_random(target, pblock=None, exclude_pblock=None, component=None) ¶

Inject a single upset at a random location.

To repeat the same locations, set the seed with configure_seed. Uses the FpgaRandomBitFlip RPC. With exclude_pblock, it also uses the FpgaExcludePblocks and FpgaIncludePblocks RPCs.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default
target TargetMemory

The memories where the upset may be injected. Several memories can be combined.

 required
pblock Optional[str]

The name of a pblock from the constraints (XDC) file. If given, the upset is injected inside that pblock.

 None
exclude_pblock Optional[Iterable[str]]

The names of pblocks from the constraints (XDC) file, for example a set. If given, the upset is not injected into the bits of these pblocks. The exclusion applies to this call only.

 None
component Optional[str]

A component of the design hierarchy, as in the net paths of the logic location (LL) file, for example "top_component/sub_component". If given, the upset is injected into a flip-flop of that component. The component must be one or more whole levels of the path. Use it with TargetMemory.FF only.

 None

Returns:

Name Type Description
FpgaRandomInjectionReport FpgaRandomInjectionReport

The location of the injected upset and, when known, the name of the affected net.

Raises:

Type Description
TypeError

If exclude_pblock is one string, or if it holds a name that is not a string.
ValueError

If exclude_pblock holds the pblock given in pblock.
DesignFileError

If a design file needed for the target or the pblocks has not been uploaded.
FrameAddressError

If the server could not exclude the pblocks, or could not include them again.
ConnectionFailedError

If the server could not inject the upset, for example because component is given with a target other than TargetMemory.FF, or the component has no flip-flops.

Examples:

>>> dev.inject_random(TargetMemory.FF, exclude_pblock={"pb_sr"})
>>> dev.inject_random(
...     TargetMemory.FF,
...     exclude_pblock={"pb_sr", "pb_sr2", "pb_sr3"},
... )
>>> report = dev.inject_random(
...     TargetMemory.FF, component="top_component/sub_component",
... )
>>> report.net_name
'top_component/sub_component/count_reg[3]'
