xadc(sensor) ¶

xadc(adc_sensor_selector: XadcSensorSelector) -> XadcSensor

xadc(drp_address: int) -> XadcSensor

Read an XADC sensor of the device.

The sensor is given either by a selector of the library, for example VCCINT or TEMPERATURE, or by the DRP address of its status register. The value is in units of the International System of Units (SI): volts (V) for voltages and degrees Celsius (degC) for temperatures.

Only the on-chip sensors, and their recorded maximum and minimum values, can be read. Uses the FpgaXadcSensor RPC.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default
sensor XadcSensorSelector | int

The selector of the sensor, or the DRP address of its status register.

 required

Returns:

Name Type Description
XadcSensor XadcSensor

The value of the sensor, in V or degC.

Raises:

Type Description
TypeError

If the sensor is neither a selector nor a DRP address.
XadcError

If the server could not read the sensor, for example because the DRP address is not a sensor, or the device does not have the sensor.

Examples:

>>> dev.xadc(VCCINT).value       # V
>>> dev.xadc(TEMPERATURE).value  # degC
>>> dev.xadc(0x01).value         # V, VCCINT by DRP address

xadc_alarm(alarm) ¶

xadc_alarm(adc_alarm_selector: XadcAlarmSelector) -> XadcAlarm

xadc_alarm(drp_address: int) -> XadcAlarm

Read an XADC alarm threshold of the device.

The threshold is given either by a selector of the library, for example TEMPERATURE_UPPER or VCCINT_LOWER, or by the DRP address of its alarm register. The server converts the raw value of the register. The value is in units of the International System of Units (SI): volts (V) for voltages and degrees Celsius (degC) for temperatures. Uses the FpgaXadcAlarm RPC.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default
alarm XadcAlarmSelector | int

The selector of the threshold, or the DRP address of its alarm register.

 required

Returns:

Name Type Description
XadcAlarm XadcAlarm

The threshold, in V or degC.

Raises:

Type Description
TypeError

If the alarm is neither a selector nor a DRP address.
XadcError

If the server could not read the threshold, for example because the DRP address is not an alarm register, or the device does not have the alarm.

Examples:

>>> dev.xadc_alarm(TEMPERATURE_UPPER).value  # degC
>>> dev.xadc_alarm(VCCINT_LOWER).value       # V

set_xadc_alarm(alarm, value) ¶

Set an XADC alarm threshold of the device.

The value is in units of the International System of Units (SI): volts (V) for voltages and degrees Celsius (degC) for temperatures. The server converts it into the raw value of the alarm register, and reads the register back to verify the write. The server keeps the bits of the register that are not part of the threshold, for example the automatic shutdown enable of OT_LIMIT, or the hysteresis or window mode of TEMPERATURE_LOWER in UltraScale+ devices. Uses the FpgaXadcSetAlarm RPC.

Caution: if the automatic shutdown is enabled, the device shuts down when the temperature is above OT_LIMIT.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default
alarm XadcAlarmSelector | int

The selector of the threshold, or the DRP address of its alarm register.

 required
value float

The threshold, in V or degC.

 required

Raises:

Type Description
TypeError

If the alarm is neither a selector nor a DRP address, or if the value is not a number.
XadcError

If the server could not set the threshold, for example because the value is outside the range of the ADC, or the design does not allow writes through JTAG.

Examples:

>>> dev.set_xadc_alarm(TEMPERATURE_UPPER, 85.0)  # degC
>>> dev.set_xadc_alarm(VCCINT_LOWER, 0.97)       # V

SkraftFpga ¶

A client for a single connection to an SK-RAFT server.

Use connect to create a client and open the connection. The class can be used as a context manager, in which case the connection is closed automatically when the block ends.

Attributes:

Name Type Description
ip str

The address of the server.
port int

The port of the server.

__init__(ip, port) ¶

Create a client without opening a connection.

Use connect instead to get a client that is ready to use.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default
ip str

The address of the server.

 required
port int

The port of the server.

 required

connect(ip, port, tls_server_cert=None, tls_cert=None, tls_key=None) classmethod ¶

Create a client and open a connection to the server.

After connecting, the server version is checked and a warning is printed if it does not match the version this client expects.

The connection uses TLS when any of the TLS files is given. This is needed when the server is started with -tls-cert and -tls-key.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default
ip str

The address of the server.

 required
port int

The port of the server.

 required
tls_server_cert Optional[str]

The path of the PEM certificate of the server (the -tls-cert of the server), used to verify the server. Its names must include the ip given here. If it is not given, the server is verified against the trusted certificates of the system.

 None
tls_cert Optional[str]

The path of the PEM certificate of this client. It is needed when the server is started with -tls-public-key, and must hold that public key. Give it together with tls_key.

 None
tls_key Optional[str]

The path of the PEM private key of this client, the private key of tls_cert.

 None

Returns:

Name Type Description
SkraftFpga 'SkraftFpga'

The connected client.

Raises:

Type Description
ValueError

If only one of tls_cert and tls_key is given.
OSError

If a TLS file cannot be read.
ConnectionFailedError

If the server cannot be reached.

skraft.datatypes ¶

Data types used by the SK-RAFT client.

Holds the options, design file settings and result types that the client sends to and receives from the SK-RAFT server.

TargetMemory ¶

Bases: IntFlag

The memories that can be selected for fault injection.

The members are flags and can be combined. Random and exhaustive injection accept combined memories. An injection at one specific location accepts at most one storage element type (FF, LUTRAM or BRAM).

Attributes:

Name Type Description
CRAM TargetMemory

The whole configuration memory, with no further limit.
ESSENTIAL_CRAM TargetMemory

Only the essential configuration bits. Needs the essential bits (EBD) file.
FF TargetMemory

Flip-flop bits. Needs the logic location (LL) file.
LUTRAM TargetMemory

LUTRAM bits. Needs the logic location (LL) file.
BRAM TargetMemory

Block RAM bits. Needs the logic location (LL) file.

required_design_files property ¶

The design files that this selection depends on.

Returns:

Type Description
tuple[str, ...]

tuple[str, ...]: The names of the Design fields that must be set. Empty if no design file is needed.

Bases: int, Enum

The ways a full readback can be done.

Attributes:

Name Type Description

A plain readback of the configuration memory.
READBACK_CAPTURE ReadbackOption

A readback that first captures the current state of all changeable elements of the device.

Bases: int, Enum

The addresses of the configuration registers of the device, for FpgaDevice.read_register and FpgaDevice.write_register.

They are copies of the register addresses of the SK-RAFT server: the ID of each register, shifted into the register address field (bit 13) of a type 1 packet header.

Attributes:

Name Type Description
FAR RegisterAddress

The frame address register.
CRC RegisterAddress

The cyclic redundancy check register.
STATUS RegisterAddress

The status register.
CTRL0 RegisterAddress

The control register 0.
MASK RegisterAddress

The masking register for CTRL0 and CTRL1.
CMD RegisterAddress

The command register.
IDCODE RegisterAddress

The device ID register.
FDRI RegisterAddress

The frame data register input, which takes the configuration data.
FDRO RegisterAddress

The frame data register output, which gives the readback data.
CTRL1 RegisterAddress

The control register 1.
COR0 RegisterAddress

The configuration option register 0.
COR1 RegisterAddress

The configuration option register 1.

Design dataclass ¶

The files of a design, as paths on the client computer.

FpgaDevice.uploadDesignToServer uploads every file that is set. All files are optional. An operation that needs a file that is not set raises an error that names the missing file.

Attributes:

Name Type Description
bit Optional[str]

The bitstream, used to program the device.
ebd Optional[str]

The essential bits file.
ll Optional[str]

The logic location file, which locates the flip-flop, LUTRAM and BRAM bits.
xdc Optional[str]

The constraints file, which declares the pblocks.
rbd Optional[str]

The readback data file, used for self-test.
msd Optional[str]

The readback mask file, used for self-test.

require(*fields) ¶

Check that the named design files are set.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default
*fields str

The names of the design files to check.

 ()

Raises:

Type Description
DesignFileError

If one or more of the named files are not set. The error message names the missing files.

FpgaComponent ¶

A component of the design hierarchy, with its flip-flops.

The server finds the components in the nets of the flip-flops in the logic location (LL) file. To inject into the flip-flops of a component, give its path as the component of FpgaDevice.inject_random. Print a component to show it and its sub components as a text tree.

Attributes:

Name Type Description
name str

The name of the component, the last level of its path.
path str

The full path of the component, for example "top_component/sub_component".
flip_flop_count int

The number of flip-flops in the component, together with its sub components.
children list[FpgaComponent]

The sub components, in the order of their names.

Examples:

>>> print(component)
top_component (120 flip-flops)
|-- other_component (40 flip-flops)
`-- sub_component (80 flip-flops)
    `-- sub_sub_component (16 flip-flops)

name property ¶

The name of the component, the last level of its path.

path property ¶

The full path of the component, to give as a component.

flip_flop_count property ¶

The number of flip-flops, together with the sub components.

children property ¶

The sub components, in the order of their names.

FpgaFiSession dataclass ¶

The settings of a fault injection campaign defined by the user.

The shares of single bit, multiple bit and multiple cell upsets are percentages and must add up to 100. A campaign can only target the whole configuration memory or its essential bits, so storage element targets are not accepted. Both rules are checked when the object is created.

Attributes:

Name Type Description
fault_type FaultType

The fault model of the campaign.
duration_ms int

How long the campaign runs, in milliseconds.
correction_time_ms int

The correction time, in milliseconds.
time_between_faults_ms int

The time between consecutive faults, in milliseconds.
sbu_percent float

The share of single bit upsets, in percent.
mbu_percent float

The share of multiple bit upsets, in percent.
mcu_percent float

The share of multiple cell upsets, in percent.
target TargetMemory

The memory to inject into. Either CRAM or ESSENTIAL_CRAM.
correct bool

If True, injected faults are corrected.
essential bool

True if the campaign targets only essential bits. Worked out from target.

essential property ¶

True if the campaign targets only essential bits.

__post_init__() ¶

Check the campaign settings after the object is created.

Raises:

Type Description
ValueError

If the upset shares do not add up to 100, or if the target is not CRAM or ESSENTIAL_CRAM.

XadcFlags ¶

The state of the XADC alarms and of the JTAG access, as read by FpgaDevice.xadc_flags from the flag register (3Fh).

An alarm attribute is True while the alarm is on. In the default mode of the sequencer, the XADC disables all the alarms, except the over-temperature alarm (UG480 and UG580, Sequencer Modes). In Zynq UltraScale+ MPSoCs, vccpint, vccpaux and vcco_ddr are the alarms of VCC_PSINTLP, VCC_PSINTFP and VCC_PSAUX.

Attributes:

Name Type Description
temperature bool

The temperature alarm (ALM0) is on.
vccint bool

The VCCINT alarm (ALM1) is on.
vccaux bool

The VCCAUX alarm (ALM2) is on.
over_temperature bool

The over-temperature alarm (OT) is on.
vccbram bool

The VCCBRAM alarm (ALM3) is on.
vccpint bool

The VCCPINT alarm (ALM4) is on, Zynq-7000 only.
vccpaux bool

The VCCPAUX alarm (ALM5) is on, Zynq-7000 only.
vcco_ddr bool

The VCCO_DDR alarm (ALM6) is on, Zynq-7000 only.
internal_reference bool

The ADC uses the on-chip reference (REF).
jtag_read_only bool

The design allows only reads of the XADC through JTAG (JTGR).
jtag_disabled bool

The design disables the JTAG access to the XADC (JTGD).

XadcRegister ¶

Bases: int, Enum

The XADC registers, at their DRP addresses, for FpgaDevice.read_xadc_register and FpgaDevice.write_xadc_register.

Only the flag register, the configuration registers and the alarm registers are accessible. The flag register is read only. The values are raw 16-bit contents. UG480 (Status Registers, Control Registers) gives the meaning of each bit, and the ADC transfer functions give the codes of the alarm thresholds. The thresholds of the Processing System (PS) supplies exist only in Zynq-7000 SoCs. FpgaDevice.xadc_alarm and FpgaDevice.set_xadc_alarm give the thresholds in SI units, and FpgaDevice.xadc_flags decodes the flag register.

The flag register shows the state of the alarms. Bit 0 is ALM0 (temperature), bit 1 is ALM1 (VCCINT), bit 2 is ALM2 (VCCAUX), bit 3 is OT (over-temperature), bit 4 is ALM3 (VCCBRAM), and bits 5 to 7 are ALM4 to ALM6 (VCCPINT, VCCPAUX, VCCO_DDR). In the default sequencer mode (CONFIG1), only OT operates. Bits 9 to 11 are REF, JTGR and JTGD.

Caution: the four least significant bits of ALARM3 select the automatic shutdown at the over-temperature (OT) limit. The value 0011b enables it.

Bases: int, Enum

The values match the frequency units that the server understands.

Attributes:

Megahertz (MHz).

JtagFrequency dataclass ¶

A JTAG clock (TCK) frequency of the FTDI, for FpgaDevice.configure_frequency.

The frequency is from 460 kHz to 15 MHz. The FTDI divides its 30 MHz clock by an integer n, from 2 to 65. Thus, it makes only the frequencies 30 MHz / n. For a different value, the FTDI uses the next higher of these frequencies. For example, 7 MHz gives 7.5 MHz and 4 MHz gives 4.29 MHz. The library defines a constant for each frequency that the FTDI makes without change, for example JTAG_15_MHZ or JTAG_500_KHZ.

Attributes:

Name Type Description
value int

The frequency, in the unit.
unit FrequencyUnit

The unit of the frequency. The default is FrequencyUnit.MHZ.

kilohertz property ¶

The frequency, in kHz.

__post_init__() ¶

Check the frequency.

Raises:

Type Description
TypeError

If the value is not an int, or if the unit is not a FrequencyUnit.
ValueError

If the frequency is not from 460 kHz to 15 MHz.

__str__() ¶

Return the frequency with its unit, for example "15 MHz".

skraft.exceptions ¶

Typed exception hierarchy for the SK-RAFT client.

All errors that the client raises derive from :class:SkraftError. Thus, callers can catch all of these errors with one except, or handle specific failures.

SkraftError ¶

Bases: Exception

The base class for all errors that the SK-RAFT client raises.

ConnectionFailedError ¶

Bases: SkraftError

The connection to the SK-RAFT server failed, or the communication with the server stopped during an operation.

DeviceReservationError ¶

Bases: SkraftError

The reservation of a target FPGA device failed. The device is not available through the selected programmer, or another process (for example, Vivado) uses the device.

DesignFileError ¶

Bases: SkraftError

A design file that the requested operation must have is not loaded, or the read or upload of a design file failed.

FrameAddressError ¶

Bases: SkraftError

A frame address (FAR) is out of range or is not valid.

BscanError ¶

Bases: SkraftError

A boundary-scan (BSCAN) operation failed.

XadcError ¶

Bases: SkraftError

The read of an XADC sensor failed.

JtagError ¶

Bases: SkraftError

The configuration of the JTAG programmer (FTDI) failed.

Changelog¶

The changes of each release of the SK-RAFT client. For the SK-RAFT server versions that the client supports, refer to Compatibility in the README.

1.0.0 (2026-11-09)¶

The first release.

Python client (api/python, package skraft)¶

  • Connect to the server, with or without TLS, list the boards and attach a board.
  • Upload a design and program the FPGA.
  • Read back the configuration frames, also with GCAPTURE, and write frames.
  • Inject into the CRAM and into the application memory (flip-flops, LUTRAM, BRAM): random, exhaustive or at one location. Limit the injection to the essential bits, to a pblock or to RTL components.
  • Count the bits of each memory, and list the frame addresses, the pblocks and the components of a design.
  • Write and read the BSCAN user registers USER1 to USER4.
  • Run external scrubbing sessions and fault-injection campaigns.
  • Read and write the configuration registers.
  • Read the XADC and System Monitor sensors, and set their alarms.
  • Set the JTAG clock (TCK) frequency and the FTDI latency: configure_jtag_frequency and configure_latency.
  • Typed exceptions, all derived from SkraftError.

Protocol¶

  • api/skraft_client.proto: the gRPC service of the server, for clients in other languages.

Examples and components¶

  • get_started/: examples 1 to 5, with prebuilt designs for the Basys 3 and the ZedBoard.
  • application_examples/: MMCM DRP interface, readback scrubbing, SEM arbitration, hardened NEORV32 SoC, TLS, XADC alarm and XADC monitor.
  • auxiliary_components/: BSCAN user registers, safe-startup clock and BRAM hold pass.

Documents and tools¶

  • docs/: concepts, general guidelines and cheat sheet.
  • docs/html-gen: builds all the documents and the API reference into one HTML file.
  • api/python/offline_bundle: an installation bundle for computers without internet access.

Python Code Style Guide¶

This document gives the conventions of the SK-RAFT Python client (api/python/skraft). Follow them in all new code, so that the client stays uniform.

All code must also follow PEP 8: four spaces for indentation, standard Python spacing. The rules below are the additional project conventions on top of PEP 8.

Every line, code or comment, is at maximum 79 columns wide. This is a hard limit, not a guideline: any line that would reach column 80 must be broken.

Write all docstrings and comments in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English, as CONTRIBUTING.md requires: short sentences, active voice, one instruction or fact in each sentence.

Examples use placeholder names. Substitute the real module, class, and function names of whatever you are working on.

1. File header¶

Every source file starts with the SPDX licence header. A blank line and the module docstring come after it:

# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
# Copyright (C) 2024-2026 SOLIDKOSMOS S.A.

"""
Short description of the module, as one sentence.

One or more paragraphs that tell what the module contains and how it is
used.
"""
  • The client is open source (Apache License 2.0). Do not use the proprietary banner of the SK-RAFT server.
  • datatypes.py and skraft_fpga.py do not have the header yet. Add it when you change one of these files.

2. Imports¶

Imports come after the module docstring, in three groups with one blank line between them:

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import os
from typing import Optional, overload

import grpc
from google.protobuf import empty_pb2

from . import skraft_client_pb2
from .datatypes import (
    Design,
    FpgaFrame,
    TargetMemory,
)
from .exceptions import (
    ConnectionFailedError,
    DesignFileError,
)
  • from __future__ import annotations is the first import of every module that has type hints.
  • The groups are: the standard library, third-party packages (grpc, google.protobuf), then the client itself.
  • Imports from the client are relative (from . import, from .datatypes import). Do not import the client by its package name from inside it.
  • Import the generated modules as modules (from . import skraft_client_pb2), and use their names with the module prefix.
  • When an import names more than one item and does not fit on one line, put the names in parentheses, one name on each line, with a trailing comma.
  • Do not use wildcard imports (from x import *).

3. Naming¶

Item Style Example
Module snake_case skraft_fpga.py, datatypes.py
Class CapWords FpgaFrame, XadcSensorSelector
Exception CapWords, ends with Error BscanError
Function, method, variable snake_case read_register, reg_addr
Constant UPPER_CASE SK_RAFT_VERSION
Enum member UPPER_CASE TargetMemory.ESSENTIAL_CRAM
Private name leading _ _rpc_detail, _UPLOAD_CHUNK_SIZE
  • Write acronyms as one word in class names: Fpga, Bscan, Xadc, not FPGA, BSCAN, XADC.
  • Give a class that mirrors a server message the prefix of its area: FpgaFrame, FpgaScrubReport, XadcSensor.
  • Put the unit at the end of the name of a quantity: duration_ms, sbu_percent, READ_PERIOD_S.
  • uploadDesignToServer and programFPGA are older names that do not follow these rules. They stay for compatibility. Do not add new camelCase names.

4. Docstrings¶

Every module, class, function, method and property has a docstring. Private helpers have one too.

The opening """ is on its own line. The first line of text is a summary, as one sentence. A blank line and the details come after it, then the sections:

def read_widget(self, widget_addr: int) -> int:
    """
    Read a widget of the device.

    Uses the FpgaReadWidget RPC.

    Parameters:
        widget_addr (int): The address of the widget, for example
            WidgetAddress.STATUS.

    Returns:
        int: The value of the widget.

    Raises:
        WidgetError: If the widget could not be read.
    """
  • The summary of a function or method is an instruction: "Read a widget of the device.", "Create a frame.", "Reserve a device by its serial number."
  • The summary of a class tells what an object of the class is: "A single 32-bit word of configuration data."
  • A property has a docstring of one line: """The value of the word.""".
  • An exception class has a docstring of one sentence that tells what failed: """A boundary-scan (BSCAN) operation failed.""".
  • Use only these section names, in this order: Parameters:, Returns:, Yields:, Raises:, Examples:. A class uses Attributes:. Do not use Args:.
  • Write each item as name (type): Description. Indent a continuation line by four more spaces.
  • In Returns:, give the type, then the description: int: The value of the widget.
  • In Raises:, give each exception that a caller can catch, and when it occurs.
  • A method that calls the server tells which RPC it uses: "Uses the FpgaReadRegister RPC."
  • Give the unit of each physical value. The client uses the International System of Units (SI): volts (V), degrees Celsius (degC), seconds, and so on.

5. Type hints¶

Every function and method has type hints for all parameters (except self and cls) and for the return value, including -> None:

def write_widget(self, widget_addr: int, value: int) -> None:
  • Use Optional[X] for a value that can be None.
  • Use the built-in generic types: list[FpgaFrame], dict[str, int], tuple[str, ...].
  • X | Y is permitted in annotations, because of from __future__ import annotations.
  • Use typing.overload when one method accepts different kinds of arguments. If the overloads give different names to the same argument, make it positional-only with /:
@overload
def read_sensor(self, selector: SensorSelector, /) -> Sensor: ...

@overload
def read_sensor(self, drp_address: int, /) -> Sensor: ...

def read_sensor(self, sensor: SensorSelector | int, /) -> Sensor:
  • The client supports Python 3.9. Do not use language features that newer versions added, for example match statements or X | Y outside annotations, such as in isinstance.

6. Classes and getters¶

Value types¶

A class that the client returns keeps its data in private, name-mangled attributes. It gives each attribute through a read-only property with the same name:

class FpgaWidget:
    """
    A widget of the device.

    Attributes:
        far (int): The frame address of the widget.
        value (int): The value of the widget.
    """

    def __init__(self, far: int, value: int):
        """
        Create a widget.

        Parameters:
            far (int): The frame address of the widget.
            value (int): The value of the widget.
        """
        self.__far = far
        self.__value = value

    @property
    def far(self) -> int:
        """The frame address of the widget."""
        return self.__far

    @property
    def value(self) -> int:
        """The value of the widget."""
        return self.__value
  • Use self.__name (two underscores) for the data of a value type.
  • Do not add setters. A value type does not change after it is created.
  • List each property under Attributes: in the class docstring.

Input types¶

A class that the user fills in and gives to the client is a @dataclass. Make it frozen=True when it does not change after it is created, as Design is. Check the values in __post_init__, and raise ValueError for a value that is not valid, as FpgaFiSession does.

Client classes¶

SkraftFpga and FpgaDevice keep their connection state in attributes with one underscore, for example self._stub. Only the client uses them. Give a value to the user through a property. FpgaDevice.serial_number, FpgaDevice.part_number, SkraftFpga.ip and SkraftFpga.port are older public attributes. Do not add new ones.

  • A class that holds a reservation or a connection is a context manager. __enter__ returns the object. __exit__ releases the reservation or closes the connection.
  • Use a @classmethod for a constructor that does more than store values, for example SkraftFpga.connect.
  • Give the gRPC stub to a helper as an argument, as BscanPrimitive.shift_in gets it. Do not store the stub in a value type.

7. Enums¶

class WidgetMode(int, Enum):
    """
    The modes of a widget.

    Attributes:
        FAST (WidgetMode): The fast mode.
        SAFE (WidgetMode): The safe mode.
    """

    FAST = skraft_client_pb2.FPGA_WIDGET_MODE_FAST
    SAFE = skraft_client_pb2.FPGA_WIDGET_MODE_SAFE
  • Use class X(int, Enum) when the user selects one value.
  • Use IntFlag when the user can combine values, as TargetMemory does.
  • When a value goes to the server, take it from the constant of the generated module, not from a number. Then the client and the server cannot disagree.

8. Errors¶

The exception hierarchy¶

All exceptions of the client are in exceptions.py. Each one derives from SkraftError, so that a caller can catch all of them with one except. Each one is for one area of failure, for example BscanError or DesignFileError. Export each one from __init__.py.

Calls to the server¶

Put each RPC call in a try block. Change a grpc.RpcError into the exception of the area, and keep the cause with from e:

try:
    request = skraft_client_pb2.FpgaReadWidgetRequest(
        addr=int(widget_addr),
    )
    reply = self._stub.FpgaReadWidget(request)

    return reply.value
except grpc.RpcError as e:
    raise WidgetError(
        f"failed to read widget {widget_addr:#04x}: {_rpc_detail(e)}"
    ) from e
  • Get the text of the server error with _rpc_detail(e).
  • Start the message with a lower-case letter, with no full stop at the end. Start it with "failed to" and tell what the client tried to do.
  • Put the values that identify the request in the message: an address, a serial number, a file name.

Errors of the caller¶

Check the arguments before the RPC call. Raise TypeError for an argument of the wrong type and ValueError for a value that is not valid. Do not send a request that is not valid to the server.

Clean-up¶

Do not ignore an error. The only exception is a clean-up step, for example _release_programmers. Tell in its docstring that it ignores errors, and why.

9. Strings¶

  • Use double quotes for strings.
  • Use f-strings to put values in a string. Do not use % or .format().
  • To break a long string, put it in parentheses and let Python join the parts. Do not use a backslash to continue a line.
raise ValueError(
    "a unit is required when the sensor is given by its "
    "DRP address"
)

10. Layout¶

  • Maximum line length: 79 columns, for code, comments and docstrings. No exceptions.
  • Break a long call or literal after the opening bracket. Put a trailing comma after the last item, and the closing bracket on its own line.
  • Two blank lines between top-level definitions. One blank line between methods. Some older parts of datatypes.py and skraft_fpga.py have one blank line between top-level definitions. Correct them when you change them.
  • Use a banner to separate groups of definitions in a long module:
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Injection selection
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
  • Inside a class, use the short form:
    # -- device acquisition ------------------------------------------------ #
  • Module constants come after the imports, each with a comment that tells what it is:
# The size of each chunk that the client streams during a design file upload.
_UPLOAD_CHUNK_SIZE = 1 << 20

11. The public API¶

__init__.py sets what a user can import from skraft:

  • Import each public name from its module.
  • Put each public name in __all__ too.
  • When you add a public class, function, constant or exception, add it to both places.

12. Generated code¶

skraft_client_pb2.py, skraft_client_pb2.pyi and skraft_client_pb2_grpc.py are generated from skraft_client.proto of the SK-RAFT server. Do not change them by hand. After each change to the .proto file, make them again with grpcio-tools:

python -m grpc_tools.protoc -I. --python_out=out --pyi_out=out \
    --grpc_python_out=out skraft_client.proto

Then change the import line in skraft_client_pb2_grpc.py to a relative import, which is the only change by hand:

from . import skraft_client_pb2 as skraft__client__pb2

Use the same grpcio-tools version as the files in the client. The generated files require at least the protobuf version that made them.

13. Comments¶

  • Write comments in Simplified Technical English, as complete sentences.
  • Tell why the code does something. The code itself shows what it does.
  • Put a comment on the line before the code it is about.
  • Use # type: ignore[code] only with a specific error code, and only when the type checker cannot know the type.

Checklist before opening a pull request¶

  • [ ] SPDX header present, then the module docstring.
  • [ ] Imports in three groups, from __future__ import annotations first, relative imports inside the client.
  • [ ] snake_case for functions, methods and variables. No new camelCase names.
  • [ ] Every module, class, function, method and property has a docstring, with Parameters:, Returns: and Raises: where they apply.
  • [ ] Every function and method has type hints, including -> None.
  • [ ] Value types keep their data in self.__name and give it through read-only properties.
  • [ ] Every RPC call changes grpc.RpcError into a SkraftError subclass, with from e.
  • [ ] New public names are in both the imports and __all__ of __init__.py.
  • [ ] Generated files are not changed by hand (except the relative import).
  • [ ] No line exceeds 79 columns.
  • [ ] Docstrings and comments are in Simplified Technical English.

Contributions¶

This repository shows the SK-RAFT Python client and the getting-started examples. Only the SolidKosmos team changes the contents of this repository.

Pull requests from persons outside SolidKosmos¶

SolidKosmos does not accept pull requests from persons outside SolidKosmos. SolidKosmos closes these pull requests without a review.

Report a bug¶

Users can report bugs through GitHub Issues. Use an issue to report a bug in the client, in the examples or in the documents.

  1. Go to the Issues tab of this repository.
  2. Click New issue.
  3. Select Bug report.
  4. Complete all the fields of the template.
  5. Click Submit new issue.

SolidKosmos examines each issue and replies in the issue.

Note: Issues are public. Do not attach confidential design files, bitstreams, EBD files, LL files or licence data. If SolidKosmos must examine a confidential design, SolidKosmos will contact you directly.

For licence questions, commercial questions or questions about the SK-RAFT server, contact SolidKosmos through www.solidkosmos.gr.

Changes by the SolidKosmos team¶

Nobody pushes changes directly to the main branch. Each change goes into main through a pull request that the repository owner approves.

  1. Make a new branch from main.
  2. Do your changes in the new branch.
  3. Write all documents and code comments in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English.
  4. Run the examples that your change affects on a board.
  5. Open a pull request to main. In the description, tell what you changed and why.
  6. Wait for the approval of the repository owner. The repository owner merges the pull request.

Add an example¶

  1. Make a new folder in get_started/, next to example1/ .. example5/ and hw/.
  2. Add a README.md to the new folder. Use the README of an existing example as a template.
  3. If the example has a new design, add the VHDL sources to get_started/hw/sources_1/new/ and the XDC files to get_started/hw/xdc/<device>/.
  4. Add the example to the table in get_started/README.md.

To add a new client, make a new folder in api/ at the root of the repository. Add a README.md to the new folder.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Company: SolidKosmos S.A.
-- SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
-- Copyright (C) 2026 SOLIDKOSMOS S.A.
--
-- Module Name: targeted_top
-- Description: Two independent heartbeat counters (slow, fast) for
--              targeted fault-injection experiments.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


library IEEE;
use IEEE.STD_LOGIC_1164.ALL;

use work.examples_utilities_pkg.all;

-- Two heartbeat modules (slow and fast) for the targeted fault-injection example

entity targeted_top is
  Generic (
    -- "7SERIES", "ULTRASCALE", or "ULTRASCALEPLUS". The value goes directly
    -- to clk_gen_wrapper.
    g_family       : string  := "7SERIES";
    -- The input clock frequency in MHz (100 MHz by default). The PLL wrapper
    -- uses it. The heartbeat intervals are in clock cycles and do not use it.
    clk_freq       : integer range 1 to 400 := 100;
    -- Maximum 5 s (500,000,000 cycles) at 100 MHz
    slow_heartbeat_interval : integer range 1 to 5*(10**8) := 1*(10**8);
    -- The default is 0.25 s at 100 MHz
    fast_heartbeat_interval : integer range 1 to 5*(10**8) := (1*(10**8))/4
  );
  Port ( 
    clk_i : in std_ulogic;
    data_o : out std_ulogic_vector(1 downto 0)
  );
end targeted_top;

architecture Structure of targeted_top is

    signal safe_clk : std_ulogic;
    
    signal heartbeat_slow_sig,
           heartbeat_fast_sig : std_ulogic := '0';
    
    component heartbeat is
      Generic (
        hb_interval : integer range 1 to 5*(10**8) := 1 
      );
      Port ( 
        clk_i : in std_ulogic;
        heartbeat_o : out std_ulogic
      );
    end component;
    
begin
    
    -- Send the input clock through the portable PLL wrapper. The period (ns)
    -- comes directly from clk_freq (MHz). Thus clk_freq is the only source
    -- for the clock frequency of the design.
    clk_gen_inst : clk_gen_wrapper
      Generic map (
        g_family          => g_family,
        g_clkin_period_ns => 1000.0 / real(clk_freq)
      )
      Port map (
        clk_i  => clk_i,
        clk_o => safe_clk,
        locked_o => open
      );

    
    slow_heartbeat:heartbeat
    Generic map (
      hb_interval => slow_heartbeat_interval
    )
    Port map ( 
      clk_i       => safe_clk,
      heartbeat_o => heartbeat_slow_sig
    );
    
    fast_heartbeat:heartbeat
    Generic map (
      hb_interval => fast_heartbeat_interval
    )
    Port map ( 
      clk_i       => safe_clk,
      heartbeat_o => heartbeat_fast_sig
    );
    
    data_o(0) <= heartbeat_slow_sig;
    data_o(1) <= heartbeat_fast_sig;

end Structure;

get_started/hw/sources_1/new/bscan_adder_top.vhd

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Company: SolidKosmos S.A.
-- SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
-- Copyright (C) 2026 SOLIDKOSMOS S.A.
--
-- Module Name: bscan_adder_top
-- Description: JTAG/BSCAN-driven adder. One BSCAN write channel (USER1)
-- supplies the operands to a simplex adder and a TMR adder. JTAG reads back
-- the simplex adder sum through USER2 and the TMR adder result through USER3.
--
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


library IEEE;
use IEEE.STD_LOGIC_1164.ALL;

library UNISIM;
use UNISIM.VComponents.all;

use work.examples_utilities_pkg.all;

entity bscan_adder_top is
  Generic (
    -- The length in bits of each operand (4 bits by default)
    op_len : integer range 1 to 32 := 4
  );
  Port (
    data_o : out std_ulogic_vector(3 downto 0) -- total_fail & min_vote(2:0)
  );
end bscan_adder_top;

architecture Structure of bscan_adder_top is

    attribute keep_hierarchy : string;
    attribute keep_hierarchy of tmr_add, sngl_add : label is "TRUE";
    attribute dont_touch : string;
    
    -- BSCAN write data path (USER1). JTAG writes the operands
    -- for the two adders.
    -- HI (7 : 4) = Op B, LO (3 : 0) = Op A (default op_len of 4)
    type bscan_ops_interface is record
        data_from_jtag  : std_ulogic_vector(op_len * 2 - 1 downto 0);
    end record;
    signal bscan_adders_ops : bscan_ops_interface;
    
    -- The XAPP1086 Isolation Design Flow specifies that the packed
    -- operands go through two separate buffers before the adders.
    -- Thus the two adders share no connections.
    signal sim_ops_buf, tmr_ops_buf :
        std_ulogic_vector(op_len * 2 - 1 downto 0);
    attribute dont_touch of sim_ops_buf, tmr_ops_buf : signal is "TRUE";
    
    -- BSCAN read data path (USER2, USER3).
    -- JTAG reads the simplex adder result through USER2
    -- and the TMR adder result through USER3.
    type bscan_result_interface is record
        -- 1 more bit for the carry bit
        data_to_jtag    : std_ulogic_vector(op_len downto 0);
    end record;
    signal bscan_sim_res : bscan_result_interface;
    signal bscan_tmr_res : bscan_result_interface;
    
    -- The examples_utilities_pkg package declares bscan_interface (see the
    -- use clause above).
    
    signal min_vote_sig   : std_ulogic_vector(2 downto 0);
    signal total_fail_sig : std_ulogic;

begin

    -- BSCAN USER1 : Write the operands for the adders
    bscan_u1_operands:bscan_interface
      Generic map (
        jtag_chain => 1,          --USER1
        data_len_r => 1, 
        data_len_w => op_len * 2,   
        -- No CDC is necessary. The adders are combinational, and only TCK
        -- clocks the BSCAN registers.
        sync       => false
      )
      Port map (
      ----- CLK INPUT FOR CDC (not used in this example) -----
        clk_i => '0',
      ----- TCK/DRCK OUTPUTS (not used in this example) -----
        tck_o => open,
        drck_o => open,
      ----- DATA PATH (WRITE THE OPERANDS ONLY) -----
        data_to_jtag_i   => (others => '0'),
        data_from_jtag_o => bscan_adders_ops.data_from_jtag,
      ----- CONTROL SIGNALS (not used in this example) ------
        ux_avail_o       => open,
        ux_ack_o         => open
      );
      
    gen_ops_lut_buf:for i in 0 to op_len * 2 - 1 generate        
        sim_lut_buf_inst : LUT1
            Generic map (
               INIT => "10")
            Port map (
               O => sim_ops_buf(i),   -- LUT general output
               I0 => bscan_adders_ops.data_from_jtag(i)  -- LUT input
            );
        tmr_lut_buf_inst : LUT1
            Generic map (
               INIT => "10")
            Port map (
               O => tmr_ops_buf(i),   -- LUT general output
               I0 => bscan_adders_ops.data_from_jtag(i)  -- LUT input
            );
    end generate gen_ops_lut_buf;
    
    sngl_add:entity work.single_adder
      Generic map (
        op_len => op_len
      )
      Port map ( 
        op_a_i =>  sim_ops_buf(op_len - 1 downto 0), -- LO Op A
        op_b_i =>  sim_ops_buf(op_len * 2 - 1 downto op_len), -- HI Op B 
        res_o  =>  bscan_sim_res.data_to_jtag  
      );
      
    tmr_add:entity work.tmr_adder
      Generic map (
        op_len => op_len
      )
      Port map ( 
        op_a_i =>  tmr_ops_buf(op_len - 1 downto 0),
        op_b_i =>  tmr_ops_buf(op_len * 2 - 1 downto op_len),
        res_o  =>  bscan_tmr_res.data_to_jtag,
        min_vote_o   => min_vote_sig,
        total_fail_o => total_fail_sig
      );
    
    -- BSCAN USER2 : Read the result of the simplex adder 
    bscan_u2_simplex_adder_res:bscan_interface
      Generic map (
        jtag_chain => 2,          --USER2
        data_len_r => op_len + 1, 
        data_len_w => 1,   
        -- No CDC is necessary. The adders are combinational, and only TCK
        -- clocks the BSCAN registers.
        sync       => false
      )
      Port map (
      ----- CLK INPUT FOR CDC (not used in this example) -----
        clk_i => '0',
      ----- TCK/DRCK OUTPUTS (not used in this example) -----
        tck_o => open,
        drck_o => open,
      ----- DATA PATH (READ THE RESULT ONLY) -----
        data_to_jtag_i   => bscan_sim_res.data_to_jtag,
        data_from_jtag_o => open,
      ----- CONTROL SIGNALS (not used in this example) ------
        ux_avail_o       => open,
        ux_ack_o         => open
      );
    
    -- BSCAN USER3 : Read the result of the TMR voter 
    bscan_u3_tmr_adder_res:bscan_interface
      Generic map (
        jtag_chain => 3,          --USER3
        data_len_r => op_len + 1, 
        data_len_w => 1,   
        -- No CDC is necessary. The adders are combinational, and only TCK
        -- clocks the BSCAN registers.
        sync       => false
      )
      Port map (
      ----- CLK INPUT FOR CDC (not used in this example) -----
        clk_i => '0',
      ----- TCK/DRCK OUTPUTS (not used in this example) -----
        tck_o => open,
        drck_o => open,
      ----- DATA PATH (READ THE RESULT ONLY) -----
        data_to_jtag_i   =>  bscan_tmr_res.data_to_jtag,
        data_from_jtag_o => open,
      ----- CONTROL SIGNALS (not used in this example) ------
        ux_avail_o       => open,
        ux_ack_o         => open
      );
      
    data_o <= total_fail_sig & min_vote_sig;

end Structure;

ff_lut_top.vhd

get_started/hw/sources_1/new/ff_lut_top.vhd

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Company: SolidKosmos S.A.
-- SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
-- Copyright (C) 2026 SOLIDKOSMOS S.A.
--
-- Module Name: ff_lut_top
-- Description: An FF shift register that operates continuously (JTAG
--              controls its clock gate) and an address-mapped LUTRAM. JTAG
--              controls and reads both through BSCAN.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

library IEEE;
use IEEE.STD_LOGIC_1164.ALL;
use IEEE.NUMERIC_STD.ALL;

library UNISIM;
use UNISIM.VComponents.all;

use work.examples_utilities_pkg.all;

entity ff_lut_top is
  Generic (
    -- "7SERIES", "ULTRASCALE", or "ULTRASCALEPLUS". The value goes directly
    -- to clk_gen_wrapper.
    g_family       : string  := "7SERIES";
    -- The length of the shift register (8 bits by default)
    sr_len         : integer range 4 to 256 := 8;
    -- The data length of each LUTRAM word (32 bits by default)
    lut_data_len   : integer range 1 to 256 := 32;
    -- Half period of the shift clock in ms (for all clk_freq values). The
    -- shift register shifts every 2 x shift_interval ms (200 ms by default).
    shift_interval : integer range 1 to 100 := 100;
    -- The clock frequency in MHz, to make the time intervals accurate
    -- (100 MHz by default)
    clk_freq       : integer range 1 to 400 := 100
  );
  Port (
    clk_i  : in std_ulogic;
    -- Bits 3:0 of the FF shift register (sr_len is 8 by default)
    data_o : out std_ulogic_vector(3 downto 0)
  );
end ff_lut_top;

architecture Behavioral of ff_lut_top is

    -- This function finds the minimum number of
    -- bits that is necessary to address the full
    -- depth of the memory array.
    function clog2(depth : positive) return natural is
        variable bits : natural := 0;
        variable val  : natural := 1;
    begin
        while val < depth loop
            val  := val * 2;
            bits := bits + 1;
        end loop;
        return bits;
    end function;

    constant time_interval : integer := shift_interval * clk_freq * 1000;

    signal safe_clk, buf_safe_clk : std_ulogic := '0';
    
    signal clk_en, clk_en_d0, clk_en_sync : std_ulogic := '0';

    -- FF Shift Register 
	signal ff_sr          : std_ulogic_vector(sr_len - 1 downto 0);
	-- div_clk - gated shift clock
	signal div_clk : std_ulogic := '0';
	-- sr_ce is the pulse that shifts the SR
	signal sr_ce                  : std_ulogic := '0';

	constant shift_period : integer := 2 * time_interval; 
	signal counter        : integer range 0 to shift_period - 1 := 0;
    
    -- LUTRAM
    constant lut_mem_depth : natural := 64;
    constant addr_width    : natural := clog2(lut_mem_depth);
    signal addr_sel : natural range 0 to lut_mem_depth - 1;
    signal wr_en    : std_ulogic := '0';
    
    -- Interface signals of the BSCAN registers

    -- BSCAN USER 1 : CLOCK ENABLE ---------------------
    type bscan_clk_en_interfacing is record
        -- JTAG reads back the clock-enable state.
        data_to_jtag   : std_ulogic_vector(0 downto 0);
        -- JTAG writes this bit to enable or disable the clock.
        data_from_jtag : std_ulogic_vector(0 downto 0);
    end record bscan_clk_en_interfacing;

    -- BSCAN USER 2 : READ SHIFT REGISTER ---------------------
    type bscan_sr_read_interfacing is record
        -- JTAG reads back the shift register state (read-only channel).
        data_to_jtag : std_ulogic_vector(sr_len - 1 downto 0);
    end record bscan_sr_read_interfacing;

	-- BSCAN USER 3 : ADDRESS SELECT ---------------------
	type bscan_addr_interfacing is record
		-- JTAG reads back the selected address.
		data_to_jtag   : std_ulogic_vector(addr_width - 1 downto 0);
		-- JTAG writes this value to select the address. The _sync copy is
		-- the same value, latched in the buf_safe_clk domain.
		data_from_jtag, data_from_jtag_sync :
			std_ulogic_vector(addr_width - 1 downto 0);
		-- New address available. The signal goes to 1 when JTAG writes a new
		-- address.
		avail          : std_ulogic;
		avail_prev     : std_ulogic;
	end record bscan_addr_interfacing;

    -- BSCAN USER 4 : READ/WRITE DATA ---------------------
    type bscan_lut_data_interfacing is record
        -- JTAG reads back the data in the selected address.
        data_to_jtag   : std_ulogic_vector(lut_data_len - 1 downto 0);
        -- JTAG writes the data into the selected address.
        data_from_jtag : std_ulogic_vector(lut_data_len - 1 downto 0);
        -- New data word available. The signal goes to 1 when JTAG
        -- writes a word.
        avail          : std_ulogic;
        avail_prev     : std_ulogic;
    end record bscan_lut_data_interfacing;

    signal bscan_clk_en_user   : bscan_clk_en_interfacing;
    signal bscan_sr_read_user  : bscan_sr_read_interfacing;
    signal bscan_addr_user     : bscan_addr_interfacing;
    signal bscan_lut_data_user : bscan_lut_data_interfacing;
    

    -- Each sr_module instance makes a circular shift register that operates
    -- continuously.
    component sr_module is
      Generic (
        mass_bit_count : integer range 0 to 512 := 8
      );
      Port ( 
        clk_i   : in std_ulogic;
        data_o  : out std_ulogic_vector(mass_bit_count - 1 downto 0)
      ); 
    end component;

    -- The examples_utilities_pkg package declares clk_gen_wrapper and
    -- bscan_interface (see the use clause above). Only sr_module and
    -- lut_memory_array have local declarations here.

    component lut_memory_array is
      Generic (
        mem_depth  : natural := 10;
        addr_width : natural := 4;
        data_len : natural := 32
      );
      Port ( 
        clk_i  : in std_ulogic;
        addr_i : in natural range 0 to mem_depth - 1;
        wr_en_i: in std_ulogic;
        din_i  : in std_ulogic_vector(data_len - 1 downto 0);
        dout_o : out std_ulogic_vector(data_len - 1 downto 0)
      );
    end component;

begin

    -- Send the input clock through the portable PLL wrapper. The period (ns)
    -- comes directly from clk_freq (MHz). Thus clk_freq is the only source
    -- for the clock frequency of the design.
    clk_gen_inst : clk_gen_wrapper
      Generic map (
        g_family          => g_family,
        g_clkin_period_ns => 1000.0 / real(clk_freq)
      )
      Port map (
        clk_i  => clk_i,
        clk_o => safe_clk,
        locked_o => open
      );
    
    -- BSCAN U1 : CLOCK ENABLE/DISABLE
    bscan_u1_clk_en:bscan_interface
      Generic map (
        jtag_chain => 1,
        data_len_r => 1,
        data_len_w => 1, -- 1 bit for the clock enable
        sync       => false
      )
      Port map ( 
      ----- CLK INPUT FOR CDC -----
        clk_i => '0',
      ----- TCK OUTPUT FOR CDC, LOGIC ISOLATION -----
        tck_o => open,
      ----- DRCK OUTPUT FOR CDC, LOGIC ISOLATION -----
        drck_o => open,
      ----- DATA PATH -----
        data_to_jtag_i   => bscan_clk_en_user.data_to_jtag,
        data_from_jtag_o => bscan_clk_en_user.data_from_jtag,
      ----- CONTROL SIGNALS ------
        ux_avail_o  => open,      
        ux_ack_o    => open    
      );
      
    clk_en <= bscan_clk_en_user.data_from_jtag(0);
     
    -- Synchronize the clock-enable signal with two flip-flops. clk_en comes
    -- from the TCK domain. The two flip-flops synchronize it to safe_clk
    -- to prevent metastability.
    sync_clk_en:process(safe_clk)
    begin
        if rising_edge(safe_clk) then
            clk_en_d0   <= clk_en; 
            clk_en_sync <= clk_en_d0;
        end if;
    end process sync_clk_en;
    
    bscan_clk_en_user.data_to_jtag(0) <= clk_en_sync;
        
    BUFGCE_inst : BUFGCE
        Port map (
           O => buf_safe_clk,   -- 1-bit output: Clock output
           CE => clk_en_sync, -- 1-bit input: Clock enable input for I0
           I => safe_clk    -- 1-bit input: Primary clock
        );
      
    -- FF SHIFT REGISTER ------------------------------------------------------
    
	-- The divider uses the gated clock. Thus it stops when JTAG sets clk_en
	-- to 0.
	-- sr_ce is a registered one-cycle pulse every shift_period cycles.
	div_proc : process(buf_safe_clk)
	begin
		if rising_edge(buf_safe_clk) then
			if counter = shift_period - 1 then
				counter <= 0;
				sr_ce   <= '1';
			else
				counter <= counter + 1;
				sr_ce   <= '0';
			end if;
		end if;
	end process div_proc;

	-- Shift clock: buf_safe_clk goes through only when sr_ce is 1.
	-- buf_safe_clk itself stops when clk_en is 0.
	BUFGCE_sr : BUFGCE
		Port map (
		   O  => div_clk,
		   CE => sr_ce,
		   I  => buf_safe_clk  
		);

	ff_sr_inst : sr_module
	  Generic map ( mass_bit_count => sr_len )
	  Port map (
		clk_i  => div_clk,
		data_o => ff_sr
	  );
    
    -- BSCAN U2 : READ SR STATE
    bscan_u2_read_sr:bscan_interface
      Generic map (
        jtag_chain => 2,
        data_len_r => sr_len,
        data_len_w => sr_len, -- not used
        sync       => false
      )
      Port map ( 
      ----- CLK INPUT FOR CDC -----
        clk_i => '0',
      ----- TCK OUTPUT FOR CDC, LOGIC ISOLATION -----
        tck_o => open,
      ----- DRCK OUTPUT FOR CDC, LOGIC ISOLATION -----
        drck_o => open,
      ----- DATA PATH -----
        data_to_jtag_i   => bscan_sr_read_user.data_to_jtag, 
        data_from_jtag_o => open,
      ----- CONTROL SIGNALS ------
        ux_avail_o  => open,      
        ux_ack_o    => open    
      );
     
     bscan_sr_read_user.data_to_jtag <= ff_sr;
     
 --------------------------------------------------------------------------

    -- LUTRAM ----------------------------------------------------------------
    -- BSCAN USER3 : ADDRESS SELECT FOR THE LUTRAM
	bscan_u3_lut_ram_address:bscan_interface
	  Generic map (
		jtag_chain => 3,
		data_len_r => addr_width,
		data_len_w => addr_width,
		-- Synchronize avail and ack to buf_safe_clk with two flip-flops
		sync       => true
	  )
	  Port map (
	  ----- CLK INPUT FOR CDC -----
		clk_i => buf_safe_clk,
	  ----- TCK OUTPUT FOR CDC, LOGIC ISOLATION -----
		tck_o => open,
	  ----- DRCK OUTPUT FOR CDC, LOGIC ISOLATION -----
		drck_o => open,
	  ----- DATA PATH -----
		data_to_jtag_i   => bscan_addr_user.data_to_jtag,
		data_from_jtag_o => bscan_addr_user.data_from_jtag,
	  ----- CONTROL SIGNALS ------
		ux_avail_o  => bscan_addr_user.avail,
		ux_ack_o    => open
	  );
	  
	  
    -- BSCAN USER4 : READ/WRITE TO THE LUTRAM
    bscan_u4_lut_ram_data:bscan_interface
      Generic map (
        jtag_chain => 4,
        data_len_r => lut_data_len,
        data_len_w => lut_data_len, -- lut_data_len bits for the data
        -- Synchronize avail and ack to buf_safe_clk with two flip-flops
        sync       => true
      )
      Port map ( 
      ----- CLK INPUT FOR CDC -----
        clk_i => buf_safe_clk,
      ----- TCK OUTPUT FOR CDC, LOGIC ISOLATION -----
        tck_o => open,
      ----- DRCK OUTPUT FOR CDC, LOGIC ISOLATION -----
        drck_o => open,
      ----- DATA PATH -----
        data_to_jtag_i   => bscan_lut_data_user.data_to_jtag,
        data_from_jtag_o => bscan_lut_data_user.data_from_jtag,
      ----- CONTROL SIGNALS ------
        ux_avail_o  => bscan_lut_data_user.avail,      
        ux_ack_o    => open    
      );

    -- Generate the CDC control for the address interface. This process
	-- captures the address in the buf_safe_clk domain on the rising edge of
	-- avail, so the LUTRAM only sees a value that is stable.
	cdc_addr:process(buf_safe_clk)
	begin
		if rising_edge(buf_safe_clk) then
			bscan_addr_user.avail_prev <= bscan_addr_user.avail;
			if bscan_addr_user.avail = '1'
			   and bscan_addr_user.avail_prev = '0' then
				bscan_addr_user.data_from_jtag_sync <=
					bscan_addr_user.data_from_jtag;
			end if;
		end if;
	end process cdc_addr;

	addr_sel <= to_integer(unsigned(bscan_addr_user.data_from_jtag_sync));
	-- Simple feedback path for debug
    bscan_addr_user.data_to_jtag <=
        std_ulogic_vector(to_unsigned(addr_sel, addr_width));
    
    -- This logic uses the same gated clock as the FF shift register path.
    -- For fault injection, all downstream fabric logic stops when clk_en is
    -- 0, not only the main demo logic. Apply this clock gate to the
    -- peripheral logic of every example. Do this even if the example is
    -- safe without it.
    sample_avail:process(buf_safe_clk)
    begin
        if rising_edge(buf_safe_clk) then
            bscan_lut_data_user.avail_prev <= bscan_lut_data_user.avail;
        end if;
    end process sample_avail;

    -- Write-enable signal for the LUTRAM.
    -- A single strobe in the buf_safe_clk domain (the gated safe_clk).
    wr_en <= '1' when bscan_lut_data_user.avail = '1'
                  and bscan_lut_data_user.avail_prev = '0' else
             '0';

    LUTRAM:lut_memory_array
      Generic map (
        mem_depth   => lut_mem_depth,
        addr_width  => addr_width,
        data_len  => lut_data_len
      )
      Port map ( 
        clk_i   => buf_safe_clk     ,
        addr_i  => addr_sel         ,
        wr_en_i => wr_en            ,
        din_i   => bscan_lut_data_user.data_from_jtag,
        dout_o  => bscan_lut_data_user.data_to_jtag
      );
    
        
    data_o <= ff_sr(3 downto 0);

end Behavioral;
