get_started/hw/sources_1/new/brams_top.vhd

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Company: SolidKosmos S.A.
-- SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
-- Copyright (C) 2026 SOLIDKOSMOS S.A.
--
-- Module Name: brams_top
-- Description: Stock Block RAM with byte-wise Hamming SEC ECC, driven over
--              independent JTAG/BSCAN address and data channels. JTAG reads
--              the stock data or the ECC-corrected data, for A/B
--              fault-injection comparison.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


library IEEE;
use IEEE.STD_LOGIC_1164.ALL;

library UNISIM;
use UNISIM.VComponents.all;

use work.examples_utilities_pkg.all;

entity brams_top is
  Generic (
    -- "7SERIES", "ULTRASCALE", or "ULTRASCALEPLUS". The value goes directly
    -- to clk_gen_wrapper.
    g_family       : string  := "7SERIES";
    -- The input clock frequency in MHz. The PLL wrapper uses it to set the
    -- PLL parameters for a correct passthrough clock.
    clk_freq       : integer range 1 to 400 := 100
  );
  Port (
    clk_i  : in std_ulogic;
    data_o : out std_ulogic_vector(3 downto 0) -- 3 byte ECC-correction flags
  );
end brams_top;

architecture Behavioral of brams_top is

    -- PLL clock, and its CE-gated version for all downstream fabric logic
    signal safe_clk, buf_safe_clk : std_ulogic;

    signal clk_en, clk_en_d0, clk_en_sync : std_ulogic := '0';

    constant bram_data_len : integer := 24; -- 3 bytes of data
    -- Bits 14:5 of the primitive address (the 10 address bits of this
    -- register) are the effective address bits, because the BRAM is 36 bits
    -- wide. The address has more than 8 bits, so the register has 16 bits
    -- (a multiple of 8).
    -- CAUTION: Keep the address value in the correct range (MAX
    -- 2**10 - 1). This design uses only bits 9:0, so a larger value
    -- accesses a lower address. All 10 bits are necessary to access the
    -- full memory array.
    constant bram_addr_len : integer := 16;
                                        
    -- Interface signals of the BSCAN registers

    -- BSCAN USER 1 : CLOCK ENABLE ---------------------
    type bscan_clk_en_interfacing is record
        -- JTAG reads back the clock-enable state.
        data_to_jtag   : std_ulogic_vector(0 downto 0);
        -- JTAG writes this bit to enable or disable the clock.
        data_from_jtag : std_ulogic_vector(0 downto 0);
    end record bscan_clk_en_interfacing;

    type bscan_address_interfacing is record
        data_to_jtag   : std_ulogic_vector(bram_addr_len - 1 downto 0);
        data_from_jtag, data_from_jtag_sync :
            std_ulogic_vector(bram_addr_len  - 1 downto 0);
        avail       : std_ulogic;
        avail_prev  : std_ulogic;
        ack         : std_ulogic;
    end record bscan_address_interfacing;
    
    type bscan_data_interfacing is record 
        data_to_jtag   : std_ulogic_vector(bram_data_len - 1 downto 0);
        data_from_jtag, data_from_jtag_sync :
            std_ulogic_vector(bram_data_len - 1 downto 0);
        avail       : std_ulogic;
        avail_prev  : std_ulogic;
        ack         : std_ulogic;
    end record bscan_data_interfacing;
    
    type bscan_ecc_interfacing is record 
        data_to_jtag   : std_ulogic_vector(0 downto 0);
        data_from_jtag, data_from_jtag_sync : std_ulogic_vector(0 downto 0);
        avail       : std_ulogic;
        avail_prev  : std_ulogic;
        ack         : std_ulogic;
    end record bscan_ecc_interfacing;
    
    
    -- The design uses all BSCAN USER registers as follows:
    -- BSCAN USER 1 : CLOCK ENABLE (freeze all downstream fabric)  --
    -- BSCAN USER 2 : STOCK BRAM ADDRESS CONTROL                   --
    -- BSCAN USER 3 : STOCK BRAM DATA READ/WRITE                   --
    -- BSCAN USER 4 : ACTIVATE ECC READ                            --
    signal bscan_clk_en_user : bscan_clk_en_interfacing;
    signal bscan_addr_user : bscan_address_interfacing;
    signal bscan_data_user : bscan_data_interfacing;
    signal bscan_ecc_r_en  : bscan_ecc_interfacing;

    -- BRAM CONTROL/DATA SIGNALS --
    signal we   : std_ulogic := '0'; -- write enable
    
    -- 4 ECC parity bits for each of the 3 bytes (12 bits)
    signal bytes_ecc_gen_pars, ecc_pars :
        std_ulogic_vector((3 * 4) - 1  downto 0);
    -- The 3 bytes with their ECC parity bits (3 * 4)
    signal data_to_bram, data_from_bram   :
        std_ulogic_vector((bram_data_len + (3 * 4)) - 1 downto 0);
    signal corr_data : std_ulogic_vector(bram_data_len - 1 downto 0);
    signal stock_data : std_ulogic_vector(bram_data_len - 1 downto 0);
    
    -- One correction flag for each byte (1 = the decoder corrected a bit)
    signal corr_bytes : std_ulogic_vector(2 downto 0);

    -- The examples_utilities_pkg package declares clk_gen_wrapper and
    -- bscan_interface (see the use clause above).
    
    -- Simple Dual-Port Block RAM wrapper, built from a direct instantiation
    -- of the RAMB36E1/E2 primitive.
    component bram_sdp_native_wrapper is
      Generic (
        -- "7SERIES", "ULTRASCALE", or "ULTRASCALEPLUS"
        g_family : string := "7SERIES"
      );
      Port (
        clk_i     : in  std_ulogic;
        en_i      : in  std_ulogic;                     -- read-port enable
        we_i      : in  std_ulogic;                     -- write-port enable
        -- 1024 words deep in the 36-bit wide configuration of this primitive
        wr_addr_i : in  std_ulogic_vector(9 downto 0);
        rd_addr_i : in  std_ulogic_vector(9 downto 0);
        -- 36 bits are used (24 data bits + 12 ECC parity bits)
        din_i     : in  std_ulogic_vector(35 downto 0);
        dout_o    : out std_ulogic_vector(35 downto 0)
      );
    end component;

    
    component secded_enc8b is
      Generic(
        data_len     : integer := 8;
        parities_len : integer := 4
      );
      Port ( 
        data_i       : in std_ulogic_vector(data_len - 1 downto 0);
        par_o        : out std_ulogic_vector(parities_len - 1 downto 0);
        ded_par_o : out std_ulogic
      );
    end component;

    component secded_dec8b is
      Generic(
        data_len     : integer := 8;
        parities_len : integer := 4
      );
      Port ( 
        data_i      : in std_ulogic_vector(data_len - 1  downto 0);
        ecc_pars_i  : in std_ulogic_vector(parities_len - 1  downto 0);  
        par_i       : in std_ulogic;
        dec_o       : out std_ulogic_vector(data_len - 1 downto 0);
        corr_bit_o  : out std_ulogic;
        uncorr_o    : out std_ulogic
      );
    end component;
    
begin
    
    safe_pll:clk_gen_wrapper
      Generic map (
        g_family          => g_family,
        g_clkin_period_ns => 1000.0 / real(clk_freq)
      )
      Port map (
        clk_i    => clk_i,
        clk_o    => safe_clk,
        locked_o => open
      );

    -- BSCAN U1 : CLOCK ENABLE/DISABLE
    bscan_u1_clk_en:bscan_interface
      Generic map (
        jtag_chain => 1,
        data_len_r => 1,
        data_len_w => 1,
        sync       => false
      )
      Port map ( 
      ----- CLK INPUT FOR CDC -----
        clk_i => '0',
      ----- TCK OUTPUT FOR CDC, LOGIC ISOLATION -----
        tck_o => open,
      ----- DRCK OUTPUT FOR CDC, LOGIC ISOLATION -----
        drck_o => open,
      ----- DATA PATH -----
        data_to_jtag_i   => bscan_clk_en_user.data_to_jtag,
        data_from_jtag_o => bscan_clk_en_user.data_from_jtag,
      ----- CONTROL SIGNALS ------
        ux_avail_o  => open,      
        ux_ack_o    => open    
      );

    clk_en <= bscan_clk_en_user.data_from_jtag(0);

    -- Synchronize the clock-enable signal with two flip-flops. clk_en comes
    -- from the TCK domain. The two flip-flops synchronize it to safe_clk
    -- to prevent metastability.
    sync_clk_en:process(safe_clk)
    begin
        if rising_edge(safe_clk) then
            clk_en_d0   <= clk_en;
            clk_en_sync <= clk_en_d0;
        end if;
    end process sync_clk_en;

    bscan_clk_en_user.data_to_jtag(0) <= clk_en_sync;

    -- For fault injection, all downstream fabric logic stops when clk_en
    -- is 0, not only the main demo logic of this example. Apply this clock
    -- gate to the peripheral logic of every example. Do this even if the
    -- example is safe without it.
    BUFGCE_inst : BUFGCE
        Port map (
           O => buf_safe_clk, -- 1-bit output: Clock output
           CE => clk_en_sync, -- 1-bit input: Clock enable input for I0
           I => safe_clk      -- 1-bit input: Primary clock
        );
    
    -- Instantiate the BSCAN USER2 register and interface for address control
    bscan_u2_addr_uri:bscan_interface
        Generic map (
          jtag_chain => 2,
          data_len_r => bram_addr_len,
          data_len_w => bram_addr_len,
          sync       => true
        )
        Port map ( 
        ----- CLK INPUT FOR CONTROL SIGNAL CDC -----
          clk_i => buf_safe_clk,
        ----- TCK OUTPUT FOR CDC, LOGIC ISOLATION -----
          tck_o => open,
        ----- DRCK OUTPUT FOR CDC, LOGIC ISOLATION -----
          drck_o => open,
        ----- DATA PATH -----
          data_to_jtag_i   => bscan_addr_user.data_to_jtag,
          data_from_jtag_o => bscan_addr_user.data_from_jtag,
        ----- CONTROL SIGNALS ------
          ux_avail_o => bscan_addr_user.avail,        
          ux_ack_o   => bscan_addr_user.ack      
        );

    
    -- Instantiate the BSCAN USER3 register and interface for data control
    bscan_u3_data_uri:bscan_interface
        Generic map (
          jtag_chain => 3,
          data_len_r => bram_data_len,
          data_len_w => bram_data_len,
          sync       => true
        )
        Port map ( 
        ----- CLK INPUT FOR CONTROL SIGNAL CDC -----
          clk_i => buf_safe_clk,
        ----- TCK OUTPUT FOR CDC, LOGIC ISOLATION -----
          tck_o => open,
        ----- DRCK OUTPUT FOR CDC, LOGIC ISOLATION -----
          drck_o => open,
        ----- DATA PATH -----
          data_to_jtag_i   => bscan_data_user.data_to_jtag,
          data_from_jtag_o => bscan_data_user.data_from_jtag,
        ----- CONTROL SIGNALS ------
          ux_avail_o => bscan_data_user.avail,        
          ux_ack_o   => bscan_data_user.ack     
        );

    -- Generate the CDC control for the address interface. Capture the
    -- address only on the rising edge of avail. At that time, the value
    -- from the TCK domain is stable.
    cdc_addr:process(buf_safe_clk)
        begin 
            if rising_edge(buf_safe_clk) then
                bscan_addr_user.avail_prev <= bscan_addr_user.avail;
                if bscan_addr_user.avail = '1'
                   and bscan_addr_user.avail_prev = '0' then
                    bscan_addr_user.data_from_jtag_sync <=
                        bscan_addr_user.data_from_jtag;
                end if;
            end if;
     end process cdc_addr;
    -- Simple feedback path for debug
    bscan_addr_user.data_to_jtag <= bscan_addr_user.data_from_jtag_sync;
    
    -- Instantiate the BSCAN USER4 register and interface for the ECC read enable
    bscan_u4_ecc_read_en:bscan_interface
        Generic map (
          jtag_chain => 4,
          data_len_r => 1,
          data_len_w => 1,
          sync       => true
        )
        Port map ( 
        ----- CLK INPUT FOR CONTROL SIGNAL CDC -----
          clk_i => buf_safe_clk,
        ----- TCK OUTPUT FOR CDC, LOGIC ISOLATION -----
          tck_o => open,
        ----- DRCK OUTPUT FOR CDC, LOGIC ISOLATION -----
          drck_o => open,
        ----- DATA PATH -----
          data_to_jtag_i   => bscan_ecc_r_en.data_to_jtag,
          data_from_jtag_o => bscan_ecc_r_en.data_from_jtag,
        ----- CONTROL SIGNALS ------
          ux_avail_o => bscan_ecc_r_en.avail,        
          ux_ack_o   => bscan_ecc_r_en.ack      
        );
    
    -- Generate the CDC control for the ECC read-enable signal. Capture the
    -- bit only on the rising edge of avail, when the value is stable.
    cdc_ecc_r:process(buf_safe_clk)
        begin 
            if rising_edge(buf_safe_clk) then
                bscan_ecc_r_en.avail_prev <= bscan_ecc_r_en.avail;
                if bscan_ecc_r_en.avail = '1'
                   and bscan_ecc_r_en.avail_prev = '0' then
                    bscan_ecc_r_en.data_from_jtag_sync <=
                        bscan_ecc_r_en.data_from_jtag;
                end if;
            end if;
     end process cdc_ecc_r;
    -- Simple feedback path for debug
    bscan_ecc_r_en.data_to_jtag <= bscan_ecc_r_en.data_from_jtag_sync;

    -- The ECC encoders use the data directly from BSCAN. Thus the parity
    -- bits are ready before the CDC process updates the synchronized data
    -- and sets the write signal.
    gen_byte_ecc_enc:for i in 0 to 2 generate
        ecc_enc_8b:secded_enc8b
          Generic map (
            data_len     => 8,
            parities_len => 4
          )
          Port map (
            data_i    =>
                bscan_data_user.data_from_jtag((8 + (8*i)) - 1 downto 8*i),
            par_o     => bytes_ecc_gen_pars((4 + (4*i)) - 1 downto 4*i),
            -- This example does not use double-error detection
            ded_par_o => open
          );
    end generate gen_byte_ecc_enc;
                                           
    -- Generate the CDC control for the data input interface. Capture the
    -- data on the rising edge of avail and make a write pulse of one
    -- cycle. Thus one JTAG write gives one BRAM write.
    cdc_data:process(buf_safe_clk)
        begin 
            if rising_edge(buf_safe_clk) then
                bscan_data_user.avail_prev <= bscan_data_user.avail;
                if bscan_data_user.avail = '1'
                   and bscan_data_user.avail_prev = '0' then
                    bscan_data_user.data_from_jtag_sync <=
                        bscan_data_user.data_from_jtag;
                    we <= '1';
                else
                    we <= '0';
                end if;
            end if;
    end process cdc_data;
    
    data_to_bram <= bytes_ecc_gen_pars & bscan_data_user.data_from_jtag_sync;
    
    
    stock_bram:bram_sdp_native_wrapper
      Generic map (
        -- "7SERIES", "ULTRASCALE", or "ULTRASCALEPLUS"
        g_family => g_family
      )
      Port map (
        clk_i     => buf_safe_clk,
        en_i      => '1',  -- read-port enable
        we_i      => we ,  -- write-port enable
        -- 1024 words deep in the 36-bit wide configuration of this primitive
        wr_addr_i => bscan_addr_user.data_from_jtag_sync(9 downto 0),
        rd_addr_i => bscan_addr_user.data_from_jtag_sync(9 downto 0),
        -- All 36 physical bits are used. The 4 parity pins (DIP/DOP) store
        -- data like the other pins, and this data goes to the decoders.
        din_i     => data_to_bram,
        dout_o    => data_from_bram
      );

    -- Connect the plain data bits (bits 23:0 of the BRAM word)
    stock_data <= data_from_bram(bram_data_len - 1 downto 0);
    -- Connect the related ECC parity bits (bits 35:24 of the BRAM word)
    ecc_pars <=
        data_from_bram((bram_data_len + (3 * 4)) - 1 downto bram_data_len);
                            
    gen_byte_ecc_dec:for i in 0 to 2 generate
        ecc_dec_8b:secded_dec8b
          Generic map (
            data_len     => 8,
            parities_len => 4
          )
          Port map ( 
            data_i     => stock_data((8 + (8*i)) - 1 downto 8*i),
            ecc_pars_i => ecc_pars((4 + (4*i)) - 1 downto 4*i),   
            par_i      => '0', 
            dec_o      => corr_data((8 + (8*i)) - 1 downto 8*i),
            corr_bit_o => corr_bytes(i), 
            uncorr_o   => open
          );
    end generate gen_byte_ecc_dec;
    
    -- Multiplex the output to BSCAN. The ECC read-enable signal selects the
    -- ECC-corrected data or the stock data.
    bscan_data_user.data_to_jtag <=
        corr_data when (bscan_ecc_r_en.data_from_jtag_sync(0) = '1') else
        stock_data;

    -- Output the ECC-correction flag of each byte (bit 3 is not used)
    data_o <= '0' & corr_bytes;
                                

end Behavioral;

bram_readback_writeback_top.vhd

get_started/hw/sources_1/new/bram_readback_writeback_top.vhd

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Company: SolidKosmos S.A.
-- SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
-- Copyright (C) 2026 SOLIDKOSMOS S.A.
--
-- Module Name: bram_readback_writeback_top
-- Description: One block RAM with the built-in ECC of the BRAM and no
--              output register, for example5.
--              The read port is always enabled. JTAG/BSCAN writes the
--              words and reads the BRAM outputs (data, ECC parity,
--              SBITERR) directly.
--
-- BSCAN registers
--   USER1  1 bit   write: clock enable (1 = runs, 0 = stopped; 0 after
--                  programming). read: the enable.
--   USER2  16 bits write: BRAM address (bits 8:0). read: the address.
--   USER3  80 bits write: bits 63:0 go to the BRAM word at the address
--                  (one write for each JTAG write). read: the BRAM
--                  outputs (bits 79:73 are 0):
--                    63:0   data (DOBDO & DOADO)
--                    71:64  ECC parity (DOPBDOP & DOPADOP)
--                    72     SBITERR
--
-- The BRAM is a RAMB36E1 in simple dual-port (SDP) mode, 512 x 72
-- (64 data bits and 8 ECC bits), with no output register (DO_REG = 0) and
-- with the built-in ECC encoder and decoder (EN_ECC_WRITE = EN_ECC_READ =
-- TRUE). Port A is the read port. It is always enabled, so the BRAM reads
-- the word at the address on each clock edge. Port B is the write port.
-- clk_gen_wrapper (safe startup) makes safe_clk from clk_i. The BRAM and
-- the BSCAN logic run on gated_clk, the output of a BUFGCE on safe_clk.
-- The USER1 enable drives its CE.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

library IEEE;
use IEEE.STD_LOGIC_1164.ALL;

library UNISIM;
use UNISIM.VComponents.all;

entity bram_readback_writeback_top is
  Generic (
    -- "7SERIES", "ULTRASCALE", or "ULTRASCALEPLUS". The value goes directly
    -- to clk_gen_wrapper. The RAMB36E1 builds only for 7-series parts.
    g_family : string                 := "7SERIES";
    -- The input clock frequency in MHz (100 MHz by default). The PLL
    -- wrapper uses it.
    clk_freq : integer range 1 to 400 := 100
  );
  Port (
    clk_i : in std_ulogic
  );
end bram_readback_writeback_top;

architecture Behavioral of bram_readback_writeback_top is

  -- Safe-startup clock from the PLL wrapper
  signal safe_clk               : std_ulogic;

  -- Clock gate: the USER1 enable, synchronized on safe_clk, drives a BUFGCE.
  signal gated_clk              : std_ulogic;
  signal clk_en_jtag, clk_en_rb : std_ulogic_vector(0 downto 0);
  signal clk_en_d0, clk_en_sync : std_ulogic := '0';

  -- USER2: address
  signal addr_from_jtag, addr_sync : std_ulogic_vector(15 downto 0) :=
    (others => '0');
  signal addr_avail, addr_avail_prev : std_ulogic := '0';

  -- USER3: write data, BRAM outputs
  signal data_from_jtag, data_sync : std_ulogic_vector(79 downto 0) :=
    (others => '0');
  signal data_to_jtag : std_ulogic_vector(79 downto 0);
  signal data_avail, data_avail_prev : std_ulogic := '0';

  -- One-cycle write pulse for each USER3 write
  signal we : std_ulogic := '0';

  -- BRAM connections
  signal bram_addr    : std_logic_vector(15 downto 0);
  signal bram_di      : std_logic_vector(63 downto 0);
  signal bram_do      : std_logic_vector(63 downto 0);
  signal bram_dop     : std_logic_vector(7 downto 0);
  signal bram_sbiterr : std_ulogic;

begin

  -- Send the input clock through the safe-startup PLL wrapper. The period
  -- (ns) comes from clk_freq (MHz).
  safe_pll : entity work.clk_gen_wrapper
    generic map (
      g_family          => g_family,
      g_clkin_period_ns => 1000.0 / real(clk_freq)
    )
    port map (
      clk_i    => clk_i,
      clk_o    => safe_clk,
      locked_o => open
    );

  -- BSCAN USER1: clock enable, 0 after programming
  bscan_u1_clk_en : entity work.bscan_interface
    generic map (
      jtag_chain => 1,
      data_len_r => 1,
      data_len_w => 1,
      sync       => false
    )
    port map (
      clk_i            => '0',
      tck_o            => open,
      drck_o           => open,
      data_to_jtag_i   => clk_en_rb,
      data_from_jtag_o => clk_en_jtag,
      ux_avail_o       => open,
      ux_ack_o         => open
    );

  -- Two flip-flops synchronize the enable from TCK to safe_clk.
  process (safe_clk)
  begin
    if rising_edge(safe_clk) then
      clk_en_d0   <= clk_en_jtag(0);
      clk_en_sync <= clk_en_d0;
    end if;
  end process;

  clk_en_rb(0) <= clk_en_sync;

  -- The clock gate. The BUFGCE output stops low.
  clk_gate : BUFGCE
    port map (
      O  => gated_clk,
      CE => clk_en_sync,
      I  => safe_clk
    );

  -- BSCAN USER2: address
  bscan_u2_addr : entity work.bscan_interface
    generic map (
      jtag_chain => 2,
      data_len_r => 16,
      data_len_w => 16,
      sync       => true
    )
    port map (
      clk_i            => gated_clk,
      tck_o            => open,
      drck_o           => open,
      data_to_jtag_i   => addr_sync,
      data_from_jtag_o => addr_from_jtag,
      ux_avail_o       => addr_avail,
      ux_ack_o         => open
    );

  -- BSCAN USER3: write data, BRAM outputs
  bscan_u3_data : entity work.bscan_interface
    generic map (
      jtag_chain => 3,
      data_len_r => 80,
      data_len_w => 80,
      sync       => true
    )
    port map (
      clk_i            => gated_clk,
      tck_o            => open,
      drck_o           => open,
      data_to_jtag_i   => data_to_jtag,
      data_from_jtag_o => data_from_jtag,
      ux_avail_o       => data_avail,
      ux_ack_o         => open
    );

  -- The BRAM outputs go directly to USER3.
  data_to_jtag <= (79 downto 73 => '0') & bram_sbiterr &
                  std_ulogic_vector(bram_dop) & std_ulogic_vector(bram_do);

  -- CDC: take each JTAG write on the rising edge of its avail signal.
  -- A USER3 write gives one write pulse (we).
  process (gated_clk)
  begin
    if rising_edge(gated_clk) then
      addr_avail_prev <= addr_avail;
      data_avail_prev <= data_avail;

      if addr_avail = '1' and addr_avail_prev = '0' then
        addr_sync <= addr_from_jtag;
      end if;

      we <= '0';
      if data_avail = '1' and data_avail_prev = '0' then
        data_sync <= data_from_jtag;
        we        <= '1';
      end if;
    end if;
  end process;

  -- The address of a 72-bit word is bits 14:6 of the primitive address.
  bram_addr <= '0' & std_logic_vector(addr_sync(8 downto 0)) & "000000";
  bram_di   <= std_logic_vector(data_sync(63 downto 0));

  bram_inst : RAMB36E1
    generic map (
      RAM_MODE      => "SDP",
      READ_WIDTH_A  => 72,
      WRITE_WIDTH_B => 72,
      WRITE_MODE_A  => "READ_FIRST",
      WRITE_MODE_B  => "READ_FIRST",
      DOA_REG       => 0,
      DOB_REG       => 0,
      EN_ECC_READ   => TRUE,
      EN_ECC_WRITE  => TRUE,
      SIM_DEVICE    => "7SERIES"
    )
    port map (
      -- Read port (A), always enabled: data on DOBDO & DOADO
      CLKARDCLK     => gated_clk,
      ADDRARDADDR   => bram_addr,
      ENARDEN       => '1',
      REGCEAREGCE   => '0',
      RSTRAMARSTRAM => '0',
      RSTREGARSTREG => '0',
      DOADO         => bram_do(31 downto 0),
      DOBDO         => bram_do(63 downto 32),
      DOPADOP       => bram_dop(3 downto 0),
      DOPBDOP       => bram_dop(7 downto 4),
      -- Write port (B): data on DIBDI & DIADI. The encoder makes the ECC
      -- bits.
      CLKBWRCLK     => gated_clk,
      ADDRBWRADDR   => bram_addr,
      ENBWREN       => we,
      WEBWE         => (others => '1'),
      DIADI         => bram_di(31 downto 0),
      DIBDI         => bram_di(63 downto 32),
      DIPADIP       => (others => '0'),
      DIPBDIP       => (others => '0'),
      -- Not used in SDP mode
      WEA           => (others => '0'),
      REGCEB        => '0',
      RSTRAMB       => '0',
      RSTREGB       => '0',
      -- No cascade, no error injection
      CASCADEINA    => '0',
      CASCADEINB    => '0',
      CASCADEOUTA   => open,
      CASCADEOUTB   => open,
      INJECTDBITERR => '0',
      INJECTSBITERR => '0',
      DBITERR       => open,
      SBITERR       => bram_sbiterr,
      ECCPARITY     => open,
      RDADDRECC     => open
    );

end Behavioral;

create_project.tcl

get_started/hw/create_project.tcl

####################################################################################
# Company: SolidKosmos S.A.
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
# Copyright (C) 2026 SOLIDKOSMOS S.A.
# Script Name: create_project.tcl
#
# Usage: vivado -mode batch -source create_project.tcl -tclargs <device> <top> [project_name] [project_dir] [-gui]
# Example: vivado -mode batch -source create_project.tcl -tclargs basys3 brams_top
# Add -gui (at any position in the arguments) to open the built project in
# the Vivado GUI at the end. The script then does not exit, and you can
# examine or change the project.
#
# The script finds the part and clk_freq of <device> and the file
# xdc/<device>/<top>.xdc. It creates the project and sets <top> as the
# synthesis top. It maps the ARCHITECTURE property of the part to g_family.
# The device_info table gives only the part and clk_freq. Then it builds
# the project to a bitstream and copies the design files to
# design_examples/<device>/<top>/ (see the end of this script).
####################################################################################

# device -> {part, clk_freq (MHz)}. The script gets the family from the part
# (see below). This table does not store the family.
array set device_info {
    basys3   {part xc7a35tcpg236-1 clk_freq 100}
    zedboard {part xc7z020clg484-1 clk_freq 100}
}
# This suite supplies and tests only basys3 (Basys 3) and zedboard
# (ZedBoard). To add your own board:
#   1. cp -r xdc/custom_template xdc/<your_board_name>
#   2. Fill the PACKAGE_PIN/IOSTANDARD placeholders in each .xdc file in
#      that folder (and the pblock SLICE/RAMB ranges, if you use pblocks).
#   3. Add an entry here, for example:
#        my_board {part xc7a100tcsg324-1 clk_freq 100}
# The build then creates design_examples/<your_board_name>/ for the files.

set known_tops {
    targeted_top
    bscan_adder_top
    ff_lut_top
    brams_top
    bram_readback_writeback_top
}

# These tops have block RAMs without an output register. Their build runs
# the BRAM hold register pass before opt_design (see
# auxiliary_components/bram_hold_pass/README.md at the root of the
# repository). The pass protects the words the design read from its BRAMs
# against the SK-RAFT accesses to BRAM content frames.
set tops_with_bram_hold {
    brams_top
}

# These tops have the g_family and clk_freq generics. bscan_adder_top has
# only the op_len generic.
set tops_with_device_generics {
    targeted_top
    ff_lut_top
    brams_top
    bram_readback_writeback_top
}

# Optional -gui flag (at any position in tclargs): open the project in the
# Vivado GUI at the end, and do not exit. You can then examine or change the
# project. The script removes the flag before it parses the positional
# arguments.
set gui_requested 0
set filtered_argv {}
foreach a $argv {
    if { $a eq "-gui" } {
        set gui_requested 1
    } else {
        lappend filtered_argv $a
    }
}
set argv $filtered_argv

proc finish {code} {
    global gui_requested
    if { $gui_requested } {
        puts "----------------------------------------------------------------------"
        puts "Opening project in the Vivado GUI for further inspection/manipulation..."
        puts "----------------------------------------------------------------------"
        start_gui
    } else {
        exit $code
    }
}

if { [llength $argv] < 2 } {
    puts "ERROR: missing required arguments."
    puts "Usage: vivado -mode batch -source create_project.tcl -tclargs <device> <top> \[project_name\] \[project_dir\] \[-gui\]"
    puts "Known devices: [lsort [array names device_info]]"
    puts "Known tops:    $known_tops"
    exit 1
}

set device    [lindex $argv 0]
set top       [lindex $argv 1]
# The default proj_name and proj_dir include the device and top names.
# Thus, two different builds never use the same project folder. Give
# arguments 3 and 4 to override them.
set proj_name "get_started_examples_${device}_${top}"
set proj_dir  "./$proj_name"

if { [llength $argv] >= 3 } { set proj_name [lindex $argv 2] }
if { [llength $argv] >= 4 } { set proj_dir  [lindex $argv 3] }

if { ![info exists device_info($device)] } {
    puts "ERROR: unknown device '$device'."
    puts "Known devices: [lsort [array names device_info]]"
    exit 1
}
set part_name        [dict get $device_info($device) part]
set device_clk_freq  [dict get $device_info($device) clk_freq]

# Get the ARCHITECTURE of the part from the Vivado part database, then map
# it to g_family. The user does not supply g_family. get_parts/get_property
# operate without a project, so a project is not necessary yet.
set part_obj [get_parts -quiet $part_name]
if { $part_obj eq "" } {
    puts "ERROR: unknown/invalid part '$part_name' for device '$device' --"
    puts "check the part name in device_info."
    exit 1
}
set part_arch [string tolower [get_property ARCHITECTURE $part_obj]]
switch -exact -- $part_arch {
    artix7 - artix7l - kintex7 - kintex7l - virtex7 - virtex7l - zynq {
        set device_family "7SERIES"
    }
    kintexu - virtexu {
        set device_family "ULTRASCALE"
    }
    kintexuplus - virtexuplus - zynquplus - zynquplusrfsoc {
        set device_family "ULTRASCALEPLUS"
    }
    default {
        puts "ERROR: part '$part_name' has ARCHITECTURE '$part_arch', which"
        puts "this suite doesn't recognize as 7SERIES/ULTRASCALE/ULTRASCALEPLUS."
        puts "Add a case for '$part_arch' to the switch in create_project.tcl."
        exit 1
    }
}

if { [lsearch -exact $known_tops $top] < 0 } {
    puts "ERROR: unknown top '$top'."
    puts "Known tops: $known_tops"
    exit 1
}

set script_dir [file dirname [file normalize [info script]]]
set src_dir    "$script_dir/sources_1/new"
set xdc_path   "$script_dir/xdc/$device/$top.xdc"

if { ![file isdirectory $src_dir] } {
    puts "ERROR: expected source directory not found: $src_dir"
    exit 1
}

if { ![file exists $xdc_path] } {
    puts "ERROR: no bundled XDC for device '$device' + top '$top' at:"
    puts "  $xdc_path"
    exit 1
}

# The shared components, relative to auxiliary_components/ at the root of
# the repository. The build uses these reference files directly.
set aux_dir [file normalize "$script_dir/../../auxiliary_components"]
set aux_files {
    bscan/bscan_interface.vhd
    bscan/bscan_primitive_wrapper.vhd
    bscan/bscan_user_register_io.vhd
    safe_clk_gen/clk_gen_wrapper.vhd
}

set vhdl_files {
    adder.vhd
    bram_sdp_native_wrapper.vhd
    targeted_top.vhd
    bscan_adder_top.vhd
    ff_lut_top.vhd
    brams_top.vhd
    bram_readback_writeback_top.vhd
    examples_utilities_pkg.vhd
    heartbeat.vhd
    lut_memory_array.vhd
    secded_dec8b.vhd
    secded_enc8b.vhd
    single_adder.vhd
    sr_module.vhd
    tmr_adder.vhd
    vec_tmr_voter.vhd
}

set missing_files {}
foreach f $vhdl_files {
    if { ![file exists "$src_dir/$f"] } {
        lappend missing_files $f
    }
}
foreach f $aux_files {
    if { ![file exists "$aux_dir/$f"] } {
        lappend missing_files "$aux_dir/$f"
    }
}
if { [llength $missing_files] > 0 } {
    puts "ERROR: missing expected source file(s) under $src_dir:"
    foreach f $missing_files { puts "  - $f" }
    exit 1
}

create_project $proj_name $proj_dir -part $part_name -force

set_property target_language     VHDL [current_project]
set_property simulator_language  VHDL [current_project]
set_property default_lib         xil_defaultlib [current_project]

set src_paths {}
foreach f $vhdl_files {
    lappend src_paths "$src_dir/$f"
}
foreach f $aux_files {
    lappend src_paths "$aux_dir/$f"
}
add_files -norecurse -fileset [get_filesets sources_1] $src_paths

add_files -fileset [get_filesets constrs_1] -norecurse $xdc_path
set_property target_constrs_file \
    [lindex [get_files -of_objects [get_filesets constrs_1] "*/[file tail $xdc_path]"] 0] \
    [get_filesets constrs_1]

set_property top $top [get_filesets sources_1]
update_compile_order -fileset sources_1

# g_family is a VHDL string generic. The value must include the literal quotes
# (g_family=\"7SERIES\"), not only the bare text. clk_freq is an integer without quotes.
set generics_set 0
if { [lsearch -exact $tops_with_device_generics $top] >= 0 } {
    set_property generic "g_family=\"$device_family\" clk_freq=$device_clk_freq" [get_filesets sources_1]
    set generics_set 1
}

puts "----------------------------------------------------------------------"
puts "Project '$proj_name' created at '$proj_dir'"
puts "Device:      $device ($part_name)"
puts "Top:         $top"
puts "Constraints: $xdc_path"
if { $generics_set } {
    puts "Generics:    g_family=$device_family clk_freq=$device_clk_freq (from device table)"
} else {
    puts "Generics:    $top has no g_family/clk_freq -- using its own VHDL defaults"
}
puts "----------------------------------------------------------------------"

launch_runs synth_1 -jobs 4
wait_on_run synth_1
if { [get_property PROGRESS [get_runs synth_1]] != "100%" } {
    puts "ERROR: synth_1 did not complete -- see $proj_dir/$proj_name.runs/synth_1/runme.log"
    finish 1
    return
}

# Always request the logic location file together with the .bit file. The
# file is harmless for the tops that do not use it (targeted_top,
# bscan_adder_top). The other tops must have it (ff_lut_top, brams_top).
set_property STEPS.WRITE_BITSTREAM.ARGS.LOGIC_LOCATION_FILE true [get_runs impl_1]

# The BRAM hold register pass, as the hook before opt_design. It writes
# bram_hold_pass.rpt in the impl_1 run directory.
set hold_hook [file normalize \
    "$script_dir/../../auxiliary_components/bram_hold_pass/bram_hold_hook.tcl"]
set use_hold [expr {[lsearch -exact $tops_with_bram_hold $top] >= 0}]
if { $use_hold } {
    if { ![file exists $hold_hook] } {
        puts "ERROR: BRAM hold pass not found: $hold_hook"
        finish 1
        return
    }
    set_property STEPS.OPT_DESIGN.TCL.PRE $hold_hook [get_runs impl_1]
}

launch_runs impl_1 -to_step write_bitstream -jobs 4
wait_on_run impl_1
if { [get_property PROGRESS [get_runs impl_1]] != "100%" } {
    puts "ERROR: impl_1 did not complete -- see $proj_dir/$proj_name.runs/impl_1/runme.log"
    finish 1
    return
}

set impl_dir  "$proj_dir/$proj_name.runs/impl_1"
if { $use_hold && [file exists "$impl_dir/bram_hold_pass.rpt"] } {
    set f [open "$impl_dir/bram_hold_pass.rpt"]
    puts [read $f]
    close $f
}
set bit_path  "$impl_dir/$top.bit"
set ebd_path  "$impl_dir/$top.ebd"
set ll_path   "$impl_dir/$top.ll"

if { ![file exists $bit_path] } {
    puts "ERROR: expected bitstream not found at $bit_path"
    finish 1
    return
}

# top -> the number of the example that uses this design.
# The script copies the design files (bit/ebd/ll and board.xdc) to
# design_examples/<device>/<top>/, next to this script. This is the same
# layout as the prebuilt files in design_examples.zip. If the folder does not
# exist (for example, for a new board), the script creates it. The script
# overwrites the files of a previous build or of the ZIP in that folder.
array set top_to_example {
    targeted_top    1
    bscan_adder_top 2
    ff_lut_top      3
    brams_top       4
    bram_readback_writeback_top 4
}

if { [info exists top_to_example($top)] } {
    set example_num  $top_to_example($top)
    set dest_dir      "$script_dir/design_examples/$device/$top"
    file mkdir $dest_dir

    file copy -force $bit_path "$dest_dir/$top.bit"
    set copied_files [list "$top.bit"]

    if { [file exists $ebd_path] } {
        file copy -force $ebd_path "$dest_dir/$top.ebd"
        lappend copied_files "$top.ebd"
    }
    if { [file exists $ll_path] } {
        file copy -force $ll_path "$dest_dir/$top.ll"
        lappend copied_files "$top.ll"
    }
    file copy -force $xdc_path "$dest_dir/board.xdc"
    lappend copied_files "board.xdc"

    puts "----------------------------------------------------------------------"
    puts "Bitstream written: $bit_path"
    puts "Example $example_num ready to run -- copied to [file normalize $dest_dir]:"
    foreach f $copied_files { puts "  - $f" }
    puts "----------------------------------------------------------------------"
} else {
    puts "----------------------------------------------------------------------"
    puts "Bitstream written: $bit_path"
    puts "NOTE: '$top' has no known example mapping -- design_examples/ not populated."
    puts "----------------------------------------------------------------------"
}

finish 0

create_project.tcl

application_examples/test_neo_hardened/create_project.tcl

################################################################################
# Company: SolidKosmos S.A.
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
# Copyright (C) 2026 SOLIDKOSMOS S.A.
# Script Name: create_project.tcl
#
# Usage: vivado -mode batch -source create_project.tcl
#            -tclargs [project_name] [project_dir] [-gui]
# Example: vivado -mode batch -source create_project.tcl
#
# The script creates the Vivado project of the NEORV32 hardening example for
# the Digilent Basys 3 and builds it, from synthesis to bitstream. It uses the
# sources and the constraints in hw/ and sets neorv32_test_setup_bootloader as
# the top. The bitstream run also writes the EBD and LL files. The default
# project is test_neo/test_neo.xpr, and neorv_fi_example/run_injection.py
# reads the .bit, .ebd and .ll files from test_neo/test_neo.runs/impl_1/.
# Add -gui (at any position in the arguments) to open the built project in
# the Vivado GUI at the end. The script then does not exit.
#
# Notes:
#   1. The sem_0 IP (Soft Error Mitigation controller) is not part of the
#      project. Add it with create_ip and generate_target if you want
#      configuration-memory scrubbing in the design.
#   2. The project does not use partial reconfiguration. If you want it, add
#      "set_property pr_flow 1 [current_project]" after create_project, and
#      set up the PR configurations and runs that the Vivado PR flow needs.
#   3. The top has a HARDEN_EN generic (default true). It switches the
#      SolidKosmos hardening of the NEORV32 core. See the comment near the end
#      of this script for the unhardened baseline.
#   4. The implementation run executes the BRAM hold register pass before
#      opt_design (auxiliary_components/bram_hold_pass at the root of the
#      repository). It protects the words the NEORV32 read from its block
#      RAMs (IMEM, DMEM) against the SK-RAFT accesses to BRAM content
#      frames. Its report is bram_hold_pass.rpt in the impl_1 directory.
################################################################################

# Target part and top. To use another board, change the part and the XDC file
# (see "Porting to a Different Board" in README.md).
set part_name  xc7a35tcpg236-1
set top        neorv32_test_setup_bootloader
set lib_name   neorv32

# Optional -gui flag (at any position in tclargs): open the project in the
# Vivado GUI at the end, and do not exit. You can then examine or change the
# project. The script removes the flag before it parses the positional
# arguments.
set gui_requested 0
set filtered_argv {}
foreach a $argv {
    if { $a eq "-gui" } {
        set gui_requested 1
    } else {
        lappend filtered_argv $a
    }
}
set argv $filtered_argv

# Exit with the code, or open the Vivado GUI if -gui was given
proc finish {code} {
    global gui_requested
    if { $gui_requested } {
        puts [string repeat "-" 70]
        puts "Opening the project in the Vivado GUI..."
        puts [string repeat "-" 70]
        # start_gui fails if the GUI is already open (script run from the GUI)
        catch { start_gui }
    } else {
        exit $code
    }
}

if { [llength $argv] > 2 } {
    puts "ERROR: too many arguments."
    puts "Usage: vivado -mode batch -source create_project.tcl\
        -tclargs \[project_name\] \[project_dir\] \[-gui\]"
    exit 1
}

set proj_name "test_neo"
set proj_dir  "./$proj_name"

# A project name without a directory gets its own default directory. Thus
# two different builds never share the same project directory.
if { [llength $argv] >= 1 } {
    set proj_name [lindex $argv 0]
    set proj_dir  "./$proj_name"
}
if { [llength $argv] >= 2 } { set proj_dir  [lindex $argv 1] }

set part_obj [get_parts -quiet $part_name]
if { $part_obj eq "" } {
    puts "ERROR: unknown/invalid part '$part_name' --"
    puts "check the part name at the top of create_project.tcl."
    exit 1
}

set script_dir [file dirname [file normalize [info script]]]
set srcs_dir   "$script_dir/hw"
set xdc_path   "$srcs_dir/xdc/basys3.xdc"

if { ![file isdirectory $srcs_dir] } {
    puts "ERROR: expected source directory not found: $srcs_dir"
    exit 1
}

if { ![file exists $xdc_path] } {
    puts "ERROR: expected constraints file not found:"
    puts "  $xdc_path"
    exit 1
}

# The VHDL sources, relative to hw/. All of them are in the VHDL library
# neorv32.
# The shared components, relative to auxiliary_components/ at the root of
# the repository. The build uses these reference files directly.
set aux_dir [file normalize "$script_dir/../../auxiliary_components"]
set aux_files {
    bscan/bscan_interface.vhd
    bscan/bscan_primitive_wrapper.vhd
    bscan/bscan_user_register_io.vhd
    safe_clk_gen/clk_gen_wrapper.vhd
}

# SolidKosmos sources: the test harness and the hardening blocks
set src_files {
    src/clk_cycle_ctrlr.vhd
    src/examples_utilities_pkg.vhd
    src/harness_controller.vhd
    src/par_checker.vhd
    src/par_generator.vhd
    src/secded_dec32b.vhd
    src/secded_dec8b.vhd
    src/secded_ecc_dec_4bit.vhd
    src/secded_ecc_enc_4bit.vhd
    src/secded_enc32b.vhd
    src/secded_enc8b.vhd
    src/tester.vhd
}
# NEORV32 core (vendored, some files modified), the NEORV32 test setup
# (the top) and the application image
set neorv32_files {
    neorv32/core/neorv32_package.vhd
    neorv32/core/neorv32_bootloader_image.vhd
    neorv32/core/neorv32_boot_rom.vhd
    neorv32/core/neorv32_bus.vhd
    neorv32/core/neorv32_prim.vhd
    neorv32/core/neorv32_cache.vhd
    neorv32/core/neorv32_cfs.vhd
    neorv32/core/neorv32_clint.vhd
    neorv32/core/neorv32_cpu_decompressor.vhd
    neorv32/core/neorv32_cpu_frontend.vhd
    neorv32/core/neorv32_cpu_control.vhd
    neorv32/core/neorv32_cpu_hwtrig.vhd
    neorv32/core/neorv32_cpu_counters.vhd
    neorv32/core/neorv32_cpu_regfile.vhd
    neorv32/core/neorv32_cpu_cp_shifter.vhd
    neorv32/core/neorv32_cpu_cp_muldiv.vhd
    neorv32/core/neorv32_cpu_cp_bitmanip.vhd
    neorv32/core/neorv32_cpu_cp_fpu.vhd
    neorv32/core/neorv32_cpu_cp_cfu.vhd
    neorv32/core/neorv32_cpu_cp_cond.vhd
    neorv32/core/neorv32_cpu_cp_crypto.vhd
    neorv32/core/neorv32_cpu_alu.vhd
    neorv32/core/neorv32_cpu_lsu.vhd
    neorv32/core/neorv32_cpu_pmp.vhd
    neorv32/core/neorv32_cpu_trace.vhd
    neorv32/core/neorv32_cpu.vhd
    neorv32/core/neorv32_debug_auth.vhd
    neorv32/core/neorv32_debug_dm.vhd
    neorv32/core/neorv32_debug_dtm.vhd
    neorv32/core/neorv32_dma.vhd
    neorv32/core/neorv32_dmem.vhd
    neorv32/core/neorv32_gpio.vhd
    neorv32/core/neorv32_gptmr.vhd
    neorv32/core/neorv32_imem.vhd
    neorv32/core/neorv32_neoled.vhd
    neorv32/core/neorv32_onewire.vhd
    neorv32/core/neorv32_pwm.vhd
    neorv32/core/neorv32_sdi.vhd
    neorv32/core/neorv32_slink.vhd
    neorv32/core/neorv32_spi.vhd
    neorv32/core/neorv32_sys.vhd
    neorv32/core/neorv32_sysinfo.vhd
    neorv32/core/neorv32_xbus.vhd
    neorv32/core/neorv32_wdt.vhd
    neorv32/core/neorv32_uart.vhd
    neorv32/core/neorv32_twi.vhd
    neorv32/core/neorv32_twd.vhd
    neorv32/core/neorv32_trng.vhd
    neorv32/core/neorv32_tracer.vhd
    neorv32/core/neorv32_top.vhd
    neorv32/neorv32_application_image.vhd
    neorv32/neorv32_test_setup_bootloader.vhd
}
set vhdl_files [concat $src_files $neorv32_files]

set missing_files {}
foreach f $vhdl_files {
    if { ![file exists "$srcs_dir/$f"] } {
        lappend missing_files $f
    }
}
foreach f $aux_files {
    if { ![file exists "$aux_dir/$f"] } {
        lappend missing_files "$aux_dir/$f"
    }
}
if { [llength $missing_files] > 0 } {
    puts "ERROR: missing expected source file(s) under $srcs_dir:"
    foreach f $missing_files { puts "  - $f" }
    exit 1
}

create_project $proj_name $proj_dir -part $part_name -force

set_property target_language     VHDL [current_project]
set_property simulator_language  VHDL [current_project]
set_property default_lib         $lib_name [current_project]
set_property enable_vhdl_2008    1 [current_project]

set src_paths {}
foreach f $vhdl_files {
    lappend src_paths "$srcs_dir/$f"
}
foreach f $aux_files {
    lappend src_paths "$aux_dir/$f"
}
add_files -norecurse -fileset [get_filesets sources_1] $src_paths
set_property library $lib_name \
    [get_files -of_objects [get_filesets sources_1]]

add_files -fileset [get_filesets constrs_1] -norecurse $xdc_path
set xdc_file [lindex [get_files -of_objects [get_filesets constrs_1] \
    "*/[file tail $xdc_path]"] 0]
set_property target_constrs_file $xdc_file [get_filesets constrs_1]

set_property top $top [get_filesets sources_1]
set_property top $top [get_filesets sim_1]
set_property top_lib $lib_name [get_filesets sim_1]
update_compile_order -fileset sources_1

puts "----------------------------------------------------------------------"
puts "Project '$proj_name' created at '$proj_dir'"
puts "Part:        $part_name"
puts "Top:         $top"
puts "Constraints: $xdc_path"
puts "----------------------------------------------------------------------"

# To build the unhardened baseline for a fault-injection comparison, remove
# the "#" of the next line. Generics are resolved at synthesis time. Thus use
# a separate project name (the first argument) for each variant, to keep both
# bitstreams.
# set_property generic HARDEN_EN=false [get_filesets sources_1]

# The bitstream run also writes the logic location (LL) file. The EBD file
# (essential bits) comes from BITSTREAM.SEU.ESSENTIALBITS in the XDC.
set_property STEPS.WRITE_BITSTREAM.ARGS.LOGIC_LOCATION_FILE true \
    [get_runs impl_1]

# The BRAM hold register pass, as the hook before opt_design. It writes
# bram_hold_pass.rpt in the impl_1 run directory.
set hold_hook [file normalize \
    "$script_dir/../../auxiliary_components/bram_hold_pass/bram_hold_hook.tcl"]
if { ![file exists $hold_hook] } {
    puts "ERROR: BRAM hold pass not found: $hold_hook"
    exit 1
}
set_property STEPS.OPT_DESIGN.TCL.PRE $hold_hook [get_runs impl_1]

launch_runs synth_1 -jobs 4
wait_on_run synth_1
if { [get_property PROGRESS [get_runs synth_1]] != "100%" } {
    puts "ERROR: synth_1 did not complete -- see\
        $proj_dir/$proj_name.runs/synth_1/runme.log"
    finish 1
    return
}

launch_runs impl_1 -to_step write_bitstream -jobs 4
wait_on_run impl_1
if { [get_property PROGRESS [get_runs impl_1]] != "100%" } {
    puts "ERROR: impl_1 did not complete -- see\
        $proj_dir/$proj_name.runs/impl_1/runme.log"
    finish 1
    return
}

set impl_dir "$proj_dir/$proj_name.runs/impl_1"
if { [file exists "$impl_dir/bram_hold_pass.rpt"] } {
    set f [open "$impl_dir/bram_hold_pass.rpt"]
    puts [read $f]
    close $f
}

# run_injection.py uploads these three files
set missing_outputs {}
foreach ext {bit ebd ll} {
    if { ![file exists "$impl_dir/$top.$ext"] } {
        lappend missing_outputs "$impl_dir/$top.$ext"
    }
}
if { [llength $missing_outputs] > 0 } {
    puts "ERROR: the build did not write these files:"
    foreach f $missing_outputs { puts "  - $f" }
    finish 1
    return
}

puts "----------------------------------------------------------------------"
puts "Bitstream, EBD and LL files written to"
puts "  $impl_dir/"
puts "Run the campaign: cd neorv_fi_example; python run_injection.py"
puts "----------------------------------------------------------------------"

finish 0
